A&M-Corpus Christi.summary: The middle blocker room emptied out: Katelyn Krienke (293.0 points), Kaitlyn Baumann (244.5) and Jaeda Rawls-Fletcher (154.5) all departed, and the lone transfer in is MB Kaitlyn Aleshire at 2.217 points per set. Everything on the pins comes back, with outside hitters Kenna Buchanan (2.755), Tatum Mason (2.527) and Logan Dyer (2.482) all returning, along with setter Virginia Van Der Werff (1.455). Eleven players return and 59% of production stays after a 13-17 season in the Southland. The final RPI was 193.

Abilene Christian.summary: Abilene Christian brings back 12 players and 85% of its production, including five of six starters and its top six scorers by points per set, led by OH Aubrey Beaver at 3.228 and MB Hannah Gonzalez at 3.154. The one hole is outside hitter Ashli Edmiston, who scored 223.5 points in 2025 and started 18 matches; the other two departures combined for far less. There are no incoming transfers and five newcomers without a Division I record, so the rebuild is internal. The 13-17 finish out of the UAC came with a final RPI of 246, and the 5-1 offense runs through returning setter Rachel Koss, who started 29 matches.

Air Force.summary: Air Force returns its top six scorers by points per set, led by outside hitter Alysa Walker at 3.833 and middle Grace Fiaseu at 2.917, with 11 players back and 61% of production returning. The losses are concentrated at two spots: Ashley Bible (457 points) and Alex Hatchett (217), both 30-match starters, leaving 2 vacancies in the starting six. With no transfers in and 9 newcomers who have no Division I record, the replacements will come from inside the program after a 15-15 season.

Akron.summary: Delaney Gash is the anchor here: an outside hitter who started all 29 matches, led the team at 4.381 points per set, and is back for 2026. The rest of the returning core is front-row heavy, with middles Lyndi Wolf (2.56 points per set) and Chidera Ozoh (2.03) also having started 29 matches. The losses are concentrated in the pins and at setter — Maureen Mathews (310.0 points) and Gabby Brissett (230.5) are gone, as is Martina Villani, who ran the 5-1. Three of six starting spots are open and 65% of production returns, with three transfers in to fill the gaps.

Alabama.summary: Alabama loses its highest-volume attacker in outside hitter Victoria Barrett, who accounted for 405.5 points in 2025 and started all 27 matches, but keeps four of six starters and 53 percent of its production. The incoming answer is transfer outside Mya Allen, whose 3.915 points per set would top the returning group ahead of Kaleigh Palmer at 2.959. Setter Hannah Parant is back after 26 starts in the 5-1, with middles Lily Gervase and Ashby Daniel also returning. The 14-13 record and No. 103 RPI finish came out of the SEC, with two spots in the starting six still open.

Alabama A&M.summary: The middle blocker room has to be rebuilt from scratch: Fatima Ramirez (375.0 points in 2025), Nisaan Martinez (332.0, now at Lamar University) and Sana Dennis (218.0) all departed, and all three started at least 28 matches. What comes back is the setter and the perimeter, with Kaydee Smith having started all 30 matches in the 5-1 and Rayishon Jackman returning at 3.763 points per set. Two transfers in headline the incoming group, including Gerren Tomlin at 3.827 points per set, but only 3 of six starters return and returning production sits at 44 percent. The 18-12 finish came with a conference tournament bid in the SWAC.

Alabama St..summary: Alabama St. loses 13 players off a 14-16 season, including OH Jyriah Morgan, whose 434.5 points were more than double the next departure's total. What comes back is the middle and the setter: Kaylen Hines (2.921 points per set) and Kamrynn Clay both started at least 25 matches and return, along with OH Taylor Williams, leaving three of six starting spots open. Returning production sits at 30 percent, with two transfers in and four newcomers who have no Division I record. The SWAC schedule ended with a No. 284 RPI and a No. 282 finish in our rankings.

Alcorn.summary: Alcorn brings back five of six starters and 67% of its production from a 2-22 season, with only one vacancy in the starting six after outside hitter Jessika Martinez departed for South Carolina St. The returning group includes the top six scorers, led by OH Courtney Carter at 2.419 points per set and MB Rylan Jones at 2.292, plus setter Juliana Henao, who started 22 matches in the 5-1. Continuity is the whole plan here: 10 players return, five left, and there are no incoming transfers. The RPI finished at 347, and the SWAC awards its NCAA bid through the conference tournament.

American.summary: Almost nothing leaves: 13 players return and returning production sits at 99 percent, with five of six starters back and no vacancies in the starting lineup. The 5-1 attack ran through outside hitter Sophie Dufour at 4.237 points per set and Salme Hollas at 3.677, both returning, while setter Deniz Dakak took AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025 and started all 28 matches. The lone departure is libero Alexandra Ioannou, who scored 14.0 points. A 24-5 record and a Patriot League tournament bid produced a final RPI of 61.

App State.summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after a 15-12 season, with nine players departed and only 32% of production returning. The losses are concentrated at the top: middle Maya Winterhoff (402.5 points), outside Ali Morris (340.5) and outside Keionna Mackey (258.5) all go, along with setter Addison Heidemann, who started all 24 matches in the 5-1. Bella Hutchens (2.983 points per set) and Lou Johnson (2.0) are the returning anchors, backed by four transfers in, including Charlotte Thompson at 2.791. The Sun Belt club finished 123rd in RPI.

Arizona.summary: Four of six starting spots are open, including setter Avery Scoggins, who started all 29 matches, and outside hitter Jordan Wilson, whose 550.5 points led the team's departures. Only 2 starters return of six and returning production sits at 37 percent, with 8 players gone and 5 transfers in to fill the gaps. Carlie Cisneros is the anchor, back after leading the team at 3.496 points per set, with middle Journey Tucker also returning. The 17-13 finish in the Big 12 came with a final RPI of 38.

Arizona St..summary: A 28-4 season and the Big 12 regular-season championship came with heavy turnover: only 2 of six starters return, leaving 4 vacancies in the starting lineup, and returning production sits at 48 percent. The departures include Bailey Miller (462.5 points), Colby Neal (278.5) and Tatum Parrott (269.5), all of whom started at least 28 matches. Noemie Glover, an AVCA First Team pick in 2025 and the team's leading scorer at 4.805 points per set, is back, and transfer Aniya Clinton arrives having scored 4.167 per set. Arizona St. finished 7th in our final rank and 6th in RPI.

Ark.-Pine Bluff.summary: A 1-28 season left Ark.-Pine Bluff at 348 in both our final rank and RPI, but almost the entire lineup is coming back: five of six starters return, leaving one vacancy in the starting six, with 76 percent of production retained. The top five scorers all return, led by MB Ashanti Butler at 2.787 points per set and OPP Zuzanna Zietek at 2.5, with setter Martyna Lubowicz back to run the 5-1. The departures are concentrated at outside hitter, where Samantha Newman (117.5 points) and Amayah Jones (87.0) both left, and there are no incoming transfers to replace them.

Arkansas.summary: Arkansas ran a 5-1 in 2025 behind setter Kiki Remensperger, who started all 27 matches, as did middles Journey Peppers and Zoi Evans; opposite Romani Thurman started 26. That continuity did not translate to results: the team went 5-22, finished 178th in RPI and 141st in our final rank, and reached the field via the conference tournament bid. Lineup data is thin in places — of 142 rotation sets resolved, only 24 agreed — and no 2026 roster is posted yet for any of the six primary starters.

Arkansas St..summary: Five of six starters return from a 22-9 season, and the outside hitter group is the reason: Kaitlin Whitlock (3.277 points per set), Devyn Lewis (2.81) and Addison Collum (2.664) are all back in the 5-1. The one hole is in the middle, where Daedrianna Cail departs after 422.5 points and 22 starts. Returning production sits at 67 percent, with 11 players back, four gone and two transfers in, including middle Ne'Khaela Rogers.

Army West Point.summary: Both outside hitters who started essentially every match are gone: Mackenzie Lynch (28 starts, 416 points... )

Auburn.summary: Auburn ran the same starting six all season — six players each started 28 matches in a 5-1 — and four of them are back for 2026, leaving two vacancies on the pins. The departures are the two outside hitters who scored most heavily besides the returning lead: Liz Markovska (392.5 points) and Bel Zimmerman (297.5). Lauren Dreves returns as the clear first option at 4.253 points per set, with Greer Chambless (2.18) and Kate Mansfield (2.078) behind her, and 57% of production comes back overall. The 17-11 record and a 54 RPI came with an SEC tournament bid; three transfers in join five newcomers with no DI record.

Austin Peay.summary: All six of the top scorers from a 5-23 season are back, headed by opposite Taly Cloyd at 3.366 points per set and outside Lauren Wallace at 2.565, which is how Austin Peay ends up with 74% returning production and 12 returning players. The losses are concentrated in two spots: middle Dayan Malave Marrero (172 points) and outside Dani Kopacz (166), leaving 4 of six starters back and two starting-six vacancies. There are no incoming transfers and six newcomers with no Division I record, so the replacements will come from inside the program. The UAC team finished 308th in our final 2025 rank and 317th in RPI.

BYU.summary: The Cougars lose outside hitter Suli Davis, who put up 591.5 points in 2025, to SMU, but they keep four of six starters and 65% of their production. Claire Little Chambers returns at 4.229 points per set, with AVCA Honorable Mention middle Brielle Kemavor at 2.798 and Sophia Callahan at 2.328; incoming transfer Dimitra Nanou scored 3.647 per set elsewhere. The 22-9 season ended at No. 18 in RPI and No. 19 in our final rank, with the Big 12 bid coming as regular-season champion. Two starting spots are open, and only two of the five departures were significant scorers.

Ball St..summary: Ball St. returns its top three scorers, all middle blockers: Gwen Crull at 2.568 points per set, Camryn Wise at 2.504 and Tiffany Snook at 2.189. The losses are on the pins, with OH Carson Tyler (581.0 points in 2025) leaving for Marquette and OH Noelle VanOort (377.5) also gone, which leaves 2 holes in the starting six and returning production at 45 percent. The team went 21-10 out of the MAC and finished 56th in RPI, reaching the field via the conference tournament. One transfer arrives, OH Audrey Geer, who scored 1.993 points per set.

Baylor.summary: Baylor loses its entire middle-blocker core and its setter: Manuela Bibinbe (310.5 points), Gabrielle Essix (237.0) and Harley Kreck (98.5) are all gone, leaving three of six starting spots open. What comes back is the perimeter scoring, led by Ksenia Rakhmanchik at 4.245 points per set and Bailey Warren at 2.795, with returning middle Victoria Davis at 2.332 after 27 starts. The 18-10 season ended at No. 23 in the RPI and produced a Big 12 regular-season championship, but 62 percent returning production with just one transfer in and six newcomers without a DI record means the 5-1 has to be rebuilt around a new setter.

Bellarmine.summary: Bellarmine brings back its top six scorers by points per set, led by outside hitter Natalie Bland at 3.538 and middle Erika Smith at 2.698, with 79% of production returning from an 11-17 season. Five of six starters return; the one vacancy is at setter, where Lillie Meinhart (136.5 points in 2025) left for Ohio, and opposite Kylie Van Hoy's team-high 162.5 points also departed. There are no incoming transfers and four newcomers without a Division I record, so the rebuild at those spots is internal. The ASUN club finished 249th in our final 2025 rank and 236th in RPI.

Belmont.summary: Belmont brings back its top six scorers by points per set, led by outside hitter Brenna Kauffeld at 2.675 and Emily Warmenhoven at 2.4, with middle Erin McMullen at 2.109. The departures are concentrated at two spots: Brooke Gilleland, who started all 28 matches and scored 438 points, and middle Bella Mathis (163.5 points), leaving two vacancies in the starting six and four starters returning. Overall returning production sits at 65 percent from a 17-11 season run out of a 5-1, with 13 players back and two transfers in.

Bethune-Cookman.summary: Bethune-Cookman returns just one of its six starters, middle blocker Kaleigh Williams, who started all 28 matches and scored 2.19 points per set. The roster turnover is close to total: 13 players departed against 4 returning, leaving 16% returning production and five vacancies in the starting six. The three biggest losses were all front-row scorers — Amya Jennings (295 points in 2025, now at Alabama A&M), Tiyanna Preston (272) and Ariel Simmons (260). Incoming transfer Alaya Rhodes leads the projected scoring at 3.075 points per set, with three newcomers carrying no DI record.

Binghamton.summary: Binghamton's top six scorers by points per set all return, led by outside hitter Viktoria Dimitrova at 3.89 and Maya Coblentz-Brown at 2.922, which is the main reason returning production sits at 65 percent. The losses are still real: Merima Smajlovic started all 22 matches and put up 390.5 points, and setter Alexandra Koleva departs from a 5-1 offense, leaving 3 of the starting six spots open. There are no transfers in and five newcomers with no Division I record, so the replacements come from inside the program. The 12-14 record finished at 203 in RPI and 234 in our final rank.

Boise St..summary: Boise St. is essentially rebuilding from scratch after a 20-11 season and a Pac-12 tournament bid: 10 players departed, only 3 return, and five of the six starting spots are vacant. The losses include OH Arianna Bilby (379.5 points), MB Layla Smith (341.0) and MB Eliza Sharp (329.5, now at Texas A&M), leaving returning production at 20 percent. OH Sydney Dreves is the one starter back, and she led the team at 2.736 points per set, with Giselle Paedon (1.815) and Kendall Hastings (1.738) also returning. Three transfers in and five newcomers with no DI record fill out a roster that finished 75th in RPI.

Boston College.summary: The middle blocker room is the story here: Anna Herrington (259.0 points) and Cornelia Roach (192.5) both depart, and Roach led the team with 30 starts. Audrey Ross returns as the clear top option at 3.935 points per set, one of three starters back from the 2025 six, with three vacancies to fill in a 5-1 offense. Returning production sits at 59 percent off a 16-16 record, and the rebuild is entirely internal — 12 players return, zero transfers in, and six newcomers with no Division I record.

Bowling Green.summary: Five of six starters return for the MAC side, including outside hitter Avery Hobson, who started all 32 matches and led the team at 3.521 points per set, with 72% of production coming back. The single vacancy is at middle blocker, where Jessica Andrews departs after 305.0 points; opposite Lauryn Hovey and her 258.5 points are also gone, though incoming transfer Karli Molnau scored 2.464 points per set. The 2025 season ended 17-15 with a final RPI of 130. Edyta Waclawczyk, at 2.922 points per set in 14 starts, is a candidate for a larger role in the 5-1.

Bradley.summary: Bradley ran a 5-1 in 2025 with a stable front-line core: outsides Gracie Furlong and Tendai Titley each started all 28 matches, and setter Maria Drapp started 27. The middle was less settled, with Mairen Mannon at 20 starts and Vitoria Oliveira at 16, while libero Megan DePoorter started 15. The 13-15 finish landed at No. 212 in our final ranking and 213 in RPI, and the MVC bid path here runs through the conference tournament. No roster information is available for 2026, so none of the 2025 starters are confirmed back.

Brown.summary: The scoring here runs through the middle: Sophia Wolfson led the team at 4.19 points per set and Fisayo Afonja added 3.048, both middle blockers, and both are back. Setter Julia Kakkis and Wolfson each started all 23 matches in a 5-1, and four of six starters return alongside 68% of production from a 14-10 season. The departures are concentrated at the pins, with outside hitter Mariia Sidorova (298.5 points) and opposite Hannah Flannery (113.0) gone, leaving two starting-six vacancies. There are no incoming transfers and six newcomers without a Division I record.

Bryant.summary: Bryant loses the pin hitter who carried its offense, Arianna Ugolini, whose 476.5 points in 2025 dwarfed every other departure, and middle London Hunt (187.0) went with her. Even so, four of six starters are back and the top four scorers all return, led by Kaitlin Curran at 2.77 points per set and Ruth Ochelli at 2.657, with setter Madison Koeller back after 26 starts in the 5-1. Returning production sits at 53 percent, and with no transfers in, the two open starting spots will have to be filled from within a group that includes seven newcomers with no DI record. The 16-12 finish came with an RPI of 220 in the America East, where the bid comes out of the conference tournament.

Bucknell.summary: Bucknell keeps its top scorer, middle blocker Sidney Shaffer, who started all 26 matches and led the team at 3.422 points per set, but has to rebuild around him elsewhere: four of the six starting spots are open and only 2 starters return. The departures are concentrated at the net, with MBs Tijana Kostic (316.0 points) and Riley Tucker (179.0, now at Tulane) and OH Bella Rodriguez (209.5) all gone, leaving 38 percent of production returning. The 12-14 finish came with a 201 RPI, and the replacement pool is thin on experience — 2 transfers in and 6 newcomers with no Division I record.

Buffalo.summary: Buffalo went 9-18 in 2025 and reached the postseason picture through the MAC's conference tournament bid. The lineup leaned on outsides Manoela Forlin (26 starts) and Emerson Matthews (25), with opposite Maddie Mitchell at 24 and a rotating middle group of Tehya Shaw (23), Ava Kanj (17) and Jordyn Romano (14). The serving order ran Chloe Brown, Matthews, Keira Kleidon, Mitchell, Forlin and Eve Adams. Roster status for 2026 is unresolved for every starter, so the returning picture is unknown rather than empty; the rank markers are 251 in our final 2025 ranking and 248 in final RPI.

Butler.summary: Butler brings back five of six starters and 70% of its production after a 12-17 season, with the one hole at outside hitter created by Alaleh Tolliver's departure to Oklahoma; she led the team with 447.5 points and started 27 matches. Elise Ward (3.514 points per set) and Sawyer Jones (2.433) return on the pins, and incoming transfer Raegan Durbin scored 3.679 points per set. The Big East team ran a 5-1 in 2025 and finished 184th in RPI. Eleven players return in total, joined by two transfers and five newcomers with no Division I record.

CSU Bakersfield.summary: The pin corps was gutted: outside hitters Nicole Zake (386.5 points in 2025), Druegan Davis (272.5) and Eva Erzen (151.0) are all gone, part of 7 departures that leave returning production at 38 percent. Suelen Lima is the one significant scorer still on hand at 3.237 points per set, with middle Nele Broszat next among returners at 1.453; transfer middle Jordyn Waite-Ward arrives at 1.959. Only 2 transfers came in and 5 newcomers have no Division I record, so the depth behind Lima is largely unproven. Bakersfield finished 6-24 with a final RPI of 301, and reaches the Big West field only through the conference tournament.

CSUN.summary: CSUN keeps both of its primary outside hitters, with Julia Bazylevych (3.177 points per set) and Hailey Brockway (3.114) back, plus middles Iye Okolo and Tatiana Turgeon, giving the Matadors four returning starters from a six-player group. The two vacancies come from opposite Leah Miller (340.0 points in 2025) and middle Hayley Ogden (279.5 points, now at Michigan St.), the top two departures among seven players lost. Returning production sits at 48 percent, with three transfers in and four newcomers who have no Division I record. The 2025 season ended 17-13 with an RPI of 180.

Cal Poly.summary: Cal Poly brings back its top four scorers, led by outside hitters Emma Fredrick (3.873 points per set) and Kendall Beshear (3.764) plus middles Chloe Leluge (2.893) and Charlotte Kelly (1.94), all of whom started at least 33 matches. That leaves 78% of production returning and only two holes in the starting six: outside hitter Annabelle Thalken, who scored 336.5 points, and setter Emme Bullis, the hub of the 5-1. The setter job is the open question, with one transfer in and five newcomers who have no Division I record. The Big West side went 27-8 and finished 42nd in RPI after taking the conference tournament bid.

Cal St. Fullerton.summary: Cal St. Fullerton keeps its top six scorers, led by middle Hannah Hass at 2.371 points per set and libero Kaia Herweg at 2.274, an unusual profile with middles and liberos filling the scoring chart. The losses are still real: MB Ketesia Hall (255.5 points) and OH Lira Pukl Verdel (210.5) are gone, leaving three of six starting spots open and 46 percent of production returning. The 5-1 offense must also replace setter Kahea Carvalho, who started seven matches. That reload follows an 8-22 season in the Big West that ended at No. 310 in RPI.

California.summary: California returns its top four scorers by points per set — Arissa Carbonara (2.551), Dominique Phills (2.429), Ashley Li (1.94) and Sawyer Thomsen (1.764) — but loses the two players who produced the most total points in 2025, middle Mikayla Hayden (341.5) and outside Peyton DeJardin (297.0), plus setter Maria Stirbu. That leaves three of six starting spots open and 50% of production returning after a 9-21 season in the ACC. The 5-1 offense will need a new setter, with 10 players back, six departed, two transfers in and four newcomers without a Division I record. The final RPI was 168.

California Baptist.summary: Emery DeJong is the offense here: the outside hitter led the team at 4.053 points per set, nearly double the next scorer, started 24 matches and is back for 2026. Four of six starters return, leaving 2 holes in the starting six after the departures of Eliana Posada (163.5 points) and Olivia Melton (152.5), both outside hitters, plus middle Jordyn Waite-Ward (119.5), who went to CSU Bakersfield. That adds up to 60% returning production off a 7-18 season in the Big West, with 9 players gone, 7 back and only 2 transfers in. The final RPI of 288 reflects how far the rebuild has to go.

Campbell.summary: Campbell won the CAA's automatic bid through the conference tournament and finished 23-7, but the roster that did it is largely gone: only 2 of six starters return, leaving 4 spots in the starting lineup open and 39 percent of production back. The departures are concentrated at outside hitter, with Gwen Wolkow (426.5 points), Maja Daca (374.0, now at UConn) and Abbie Tuyo (169.5, now at Jacksonville) all out. Setter Hannah Pattie, who started 29 matches, returns to run the 5-1, with middle Hailey Heytvelt (2.15 points per set) back alongside her. Transfer outside Emma McCartney arrives as the highest scorer on the roster at 3.35 points per set, one of just 2 transfers in among six newcomers with no DI record.

Canisius.summary: Canisius returns its entire outside hitter corps — Emma Isroff (2.856 points per set), Madi Cowan (2.721) and Julia Lenik (2.595) are all back — but loses both starting middles and the setter, leaving 3 starting-six vacancies and only 2 of six starters returning. Bella Mosquera (405 points in 2025) and Kalia Reisma (227) are the departures to replace in the middle, and with 0 transfers in and 5 newcomers without a DI record, the rebuild is internal. The 5-1 offense went 12-18 last season, finishing 295th in RPI. Returning production sits at 60 percent, weighted heavily toward the pins.

Central Ark..summary: Central Ark. loses its entire outside hitter core and its setter: Laci Bohannan (440.5 points), Gabby Tuiaana (365.5) and Samantha Cousins (210.0) are all gone, along with Caylan Koons, who started 29 matches at setter. That leaves 34% returning production and three of six starting spots open after an 18-12 season that ended with a UAC tournament bid. The rebuild leans on middles McKinzee Haas (2.261 points per set) and Greyson Button (2.089), plus four transfers in, headlined by projected top scorer Fiona Vandyke at 3.268 points per set. The 5-1 offense will need a new setter to run it.

Central Conn. St..summary: Central Conn. St. ran a 5-1 in 2025 and leaned on a fixed group: four players — middle Amanda Tokam, setter Anja Milosevic, opposite Olivia Keckler and outside Weronika Poczynek — each started all 27 matches with a known lineup, with middle Breanna Ginley at 26 and libero-side Gabriella Burdier at 18. The lineup data is thin in places, though: of 140 rotation sets resolved, only 30 agreed. The team went 9-19, finishing 334th in our final rank and 336th in RPI, and reached the NCAA field via the NEC conference tournament. No 2026 roster is posted yet for any of those starters.

Central Mich..summary: Central Mich. is essentially starting over: 12 players departed and only 3 return, leaving 19% of production and five of six starting spots open. The one anchor is OH Taylor Cripe, who started 23 matches and led the team at 3.15 points per set. Everything else that carried the 5-1 offense is gone, including Natalia Rejment (273 points), Grace Thomas (273) and Abby Olin (246), with 3 transfers in and 7 newcomers who have no DI record. The 2025 season finished 9-21, with an RPI of 245 in the MAC.

Charleston So..summary: Charleston So. has four of its six starting spots to fill after losing outside hitter Skylar Yates (364.5 points in 2025) and middle Emily Struckmeyer, both of whom started all 29 matches, plus outside Oliwia Durka. Only two starters return, and returning production sits at 39 percent from a 16-13 season. The pieces still in place are middle Emma Bednarek, the team's top scorer at 2.505 points per set, and outsides Faith Burch (2.129) and Emersyn Reiter (2.076), with setter Tristin Sutton back after 21 starts in the 5-1. The roster adds one transfer and four newcomers without a Division I record.

Charlotte.summary: Charlotte returns just one of six starters and 10% of its production after 11 players departed, including all three outside hitters who started all 29 matches — Kristen Birmingham (464.5 points), Jessica Ricks (427.5) and Jaylen Jordan (254.0). That leaves five vacancies in the starting six, to be filled by five transfers in and five newcomers with no Division I record. Middle blocker Jovana Antic, at 1.548 points per set, is the top returner; projected leading scorer Gia McGrew (2.089) is a transfer. The 17-12 season ended with an American bid via the conference tournament, an RPI of 125 and a final rank of 133.

Chattanooga.summary: Chattanooga keeps its top three scorers by points per set — Gracie Rose (2.907), Kynli Kirkendoll (2.718) and Jordin Glass (2.069) — after going 16-13 and reaching the NCAA field through the SoCon tournament. The losses are concentrated on the pin: Sydney Jackwin, who scored 437.5 points in 2025 and started all 29 matches, plus fellow outside Kendyl MacAskill (184.5 points). Four of six starters return and returning production sits at 58 percent, leaving two spots in the starting lineup open. Setter Ashley Reynolds is back after 21 starts, and transfer Sophia Garrido arrives with 2.06 points per set.

Chicago St..summary: Eight players departed and only three return, leaving four vacancies in the starting six and just one returning starter. The losses are concentrated at the pins: Zeynep Ertam (232.0 points in 2025) and Jocelyn Carter (164.5) were both outside hitters, with opposite Leah Linares Castro (128.0) also gone. Nayella George is the one significant piece back, having led the team at 2.822 points per set, with Gracilove Littlejohn (1.241) next. After a 1-25 season that ended at No. 343 in RPI, one transfer in and 33 percent returning production leave most of the lineup unsettled.

Cincinnati.summary: Three of last year's top six starters are back, but the three vacancies include Carly Glendinning, who led the team with 413.0 points before departing, and fellow outside Gretchen Sigman (251.5 points, now at Texas Tech). Setter Andi Spies started all 26 matches in the 5-1 and returns alongside Sydney Nolan, whose 5.07 points per set led the team. Incoming transfers Andrea Simovski (3.365 points per set) and Audrey Rome (2.829) are candidates to fill the open outside and middle spots. The 15-13 record finished at No. 53 in RPI, with returning production at 48 percent.

Clemson.summary: Four of the six starting spots from the 18-14 season are open, with only setter Katherine Sandt and libero Addi Rains back among the regulars and returning production sitting at 28 percent. The losses are the whole front-line scoring core: Mia McGrath (387.5 points), Kate Hansen (309.5, now at Purdue) and Mia Moore (268.5). The rebuild leans on Kennedy Wagner, who returns after 4.306 points per set, plus four transfers in, three of whom rank among the projected top scorers. The 5-1 was the system in 2025, and the group finished 94th in RPI.

Cleveland St..summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after a 6-23 season, with outside hitter Laken Voss (312.5 points, 27 starts) the largest departure among six players gone. What's left is a middle-heavy core: Bryn VanVleet returns at 3.134 points per set from the outside, with middles Julia Jozefov (1.974) and JeriLynn Koehler (1.709) behind her, and returning production sits at 52 percent. The rebuild leans on eight newcomers with no Division I record and just two transfers in, which is thin cover for that many vacancies. The Horizon program finished 304th in RPI.

Coastal Carolina.summary: Nine departures against six returners leaves this Sun Belt group at 31% returning production, including setter Jalyn Stout (408 points in 2025) and outside hitters Emily Fowler (336) and Emma Van Elslande (256), who filled three of the six serving-rotation slots. The rebuild leans on four transfers, with Hatteras Welker at 3.188 points per set expected to headline a middle-heavy attack alongside returning MB Anna Rita (2.626) and OH Anzley Rinard (2.428). Coastal Carolina went 18-11 last year and finished 95th in final RPI, 104th in our own rank, reaching the field through the conference tournament.

Col. of Charleston.summary: Five of six starters are back from an 18-10 season, with 73% of production returning, so the only real hole is at outside hitter where Izzy Marinelli left after 395.5 points and 27 starts. The incoming piece is a big one: transfer RS Gabby Tuiaana would lead the team at 3.514 points per set, just ahead of returning MB Caroline Noonan at 3.455. Setter Lauren Dow returns having started all 27 matches in a 5-1, and the CAA club finished 116th in RPI against a final rank of 146.

Colgate.summary: Colgate went 18-10 in 2025 and reached the NCAA field through the Patriot League tournament. Outside hitter Milan Bayless, an AVCA Honorable Mention in 2024, started all 28 matches, with middles Maddie Rudolph (27 starts) and Lal Akin (26) alongside her; setting duties were split between Jordyn Moore (15 starts) and Ava Schabes (14). The lineup data is thin in places — only 33 of 150 rotation sets agreed — and no 2026 roster information is available for any of the six primary starters.

Colorado.summary: Colorado brings back 5 of six starters and 88% of its production from a 23-9 season, with the lone vacancy at setter after Rian Finley's departure. Ana Burilović anchors the attack at 5.433 points per set, well clear of Sydney Jordan at 2.962 and Cayla Payne at 2.756, and all three return. The Big 12 side earned its bid as regular-season champion and finished 22nd in RPI; the open setter spot in a 5-1 is the one real question, with 11 players returning and just one transfer in.

Colorado St..summary: Colorado St. brings back all six starters and 89% of its production after a 21-9 season, with no vacancies in the starting six. The middle is the strength: Eve Wilson led the team at 3.648 points per set and started all 30 matches, with Kekua Richards (3.086) and Brenna Rowland (2.273) also returning inside, alongside outsides Maria Brun (3.383) and Halle Jameson (3.137) and setter Erin Debiec in the 5-1. The departures are outside hitter Riley Simpson (81.0 points in 2025), middle Jazen Debina (80.0, to Cleveland St.) and libero Aine Doty (28.0), with one transfer in and five newcomers who have no Division I record.

Columbia.summary: Columbia went 2-22 in 2025 but keeps almost everything: five of six starters return, 63% of production comes back, and the only departure from the starting lineup is libero Presley Liberty. The top six scorers are all returning, led by outside hitter Elena Maynulet at 3.304 points per set and middle Maria Happ at 2.294. The biggest loss is opposite Eva Atkins and her 243.0 points, and with 0 transfers in the Ivy League team will fill that gap internally. Rankings were 328 in our final poll and 331 in RPI.

Coppin St..summary: Coppin St. went 23-12 and took the MEAC's bid through the conference tournament, but the roster turns over hard: nine players departed, including outside hitter TaKenya Stafford, whose 550.0 points led the team by a wide margin. Three of the six starting spots are open, with middle Ahzhi Coleman (175.5 points) and setter Ayanna Pharoah (143.0) also gone. What comes back is the top returning scorer, OH Cherisse Atilano at 3.141 points per set, along with Kayden Cupid (2.226) and Ivanna Luna (2.026), which holds returning production at 52 percent. Only one transfer arrives, and four newcomers have no DI record.

Cornell.summary: Cornell's returning core is its middles: Mackenzie Parsons (3.296 points per set) and Ava Bogan (2.25) both started all 25 matches and are back, while all four outside hitters and the setter who started are gone, leaving four holes in the starting six. The outside losses are heavy, led by Eliza Konvicka's 403.5 points in 2025. With 11 players returning, no transfers in, and 47 percent of production back, the rebuild leans on Haley Clark (2.023 points per set) and Jaida Sione (1.381) to absorb the pin work after a 15-10 season.

Creighton.summary: Creighton loses its entire left side of the setter-outside-middle spine: Annalea Maeder, Ava Martin and Kiara Reinhardt each started all 33 matches and all three are gone, with Martin's 595.5 points in 2025 the largest single departure. That leaves three starting-six vacancies and 44% returning production off a 28-6 season that finished 7th in RPI. The returning scoring is led by Jaya Johnson at 2.894 points per set, with Abbey Hayes (2.161) and Eloise Brandewie (1.975) also back, and three transfers arrive to fill the rest.

Dartmouth.summary: Every one of the top six scorers from 2025 is back, led by Maddie LaFata at 2.75 points per set, Elle McCreery at 1.918 and Zori Brown at 1.894. The exception is outside hitter Kauany Gutz, whose 288.0 points and 22 starts leave the largest hole, with middle blockers Ava Roberts and Molly Power also gone; four of six starters return and two starting-six spots are open. Setter Sophia Gagnepain ran the 5-1 and started 21 matches, so continuity at the position is intact. There were no transfers in, so the 7-17 record has to improve from internal development.

Davidson.summary: Five of six starters return from a 12-16 season, and the returning group includes each of the top six scorers, led by outside hitter Elena Garcia-Guerrios at 4.068 points per set and Meile Songaila at 2.753. Returning production sits at 78 percent, with the only real hole left by outside hitter Anna Withee, whose 160 points were the largest departure. The 5-1 offense stays in place with setter Kinsey Smith, who started 23 matches. The Atlantic 10 side finished 215th in RPI, and its path to a bid runs through the conference tournament.

Dayton.summary: Dayton returns its best attacker in Kamryn Hunt, an AVCA Honorable Mention pick in 2025 who led the team at 4.519 points per set and started 28 matches. The roster turns over hard around her: 11 players departed against 7 returning, three of six starting spots are open, and returning production sits at 49 percent. The losses are concentrated up the middle and at setter, with MB Liana Sarkissian (312.0 points) and setter Viktoria Wahlgren (188.5) both gone. Four transfers arrive, including OH Kaleigh Meritt at 4.125 points per set, after a 23-7 season that finished 50th in final RPI.

DePaul.summary: DePaul brings back its top six scorers, including Kendall Timme at 3.859 points per set, Isabela Tavares Salomon at 3.611 and Morgan Stewart at 3.224, which is the core of 76 percent returning production. The one real hole is in the middle: Katelynn Oxley, a 27-match starter who accounted for 277.0 points, is gone, leaving one vacancy in the starting six and four of six starters back. The 5-1 ran through setter Amanda Saeger, who started 25 matches and is returning. A 14-13 season produced an RPI of 150 and a final ranking of 160, with only one transfer in.

Delaware.summary: All three of the top scorers are back, led by Anna Logan Gillens at 3.473 points per set, with Asia Murray (2.371) and Jayda Redd (2.348) behind her. Four of six starters return and returning production sits at 65 percent, though the departures of Dylan Norris (215.5 points in 2025) and Sila Ozyurek (114.0) leave two holes in the starting six, at opposite and middle. The 5-1 offense stays intact with setter Kennedi Inman, who started 20 matches. An 8-17 season and a final RPI of 259 set a low bar, and only one transfer was added to clear it.

Delaware St..summary: The top three scorers all return: Aaliyah Mitchell at 3.125 points per set, Emma Patmon at 2.534 and middle Hannah Sanders at 1.856, which is the core of a 55% returning production figure. The losses are concentrated in two spots — Gerren Tomlin (398 points, off to Alabama A&M) and Kelsie Dawson (192) both started 24 matches, leaving 2 vacancies in the starting six. Delaware St. went 12-18 in the MEAC and finished 287th in RPI, running a 5-1. Eleven players return against nine departures, with 3 transfers in.

Denver.summary: Denver enters 2026 having to replace three of its six starters, including outside hitter Ava Reynolds (352 points in 2025) and opposite Genevieve Lewis (294), leaving returning production at 44 percent. What does come back is the top of the scoring chart: Jamia Johnson (2.56 points per set), Alicia Thibodeau (2.418) and Izabela Molina (2.05) are all returning. The 2025 group went 17-11 out of the 5-1, finished 124th in our final rank and 139th in RPI, and the roster reload leans on one transfer in and five newcomers with no Division I record.

Drake.summary: Drake loses three of its six regular starters, including outside hitter Macy Daufeldt (452.5 points in 2025) and middle Kacia Brown (426.0), plus setter Addison Beagle, which leaves the 5-1 without its primary distributor. What comes back is real, though: Caroline Smith (2.331 points per set) and Bliss Beck (2.22) both return, and four transfers in include Matthea Dalton at 2.068 and Hannah Ditsworth at 1.864. Returning production sits at 50 percent with eight players back and eight gone, and the MVC side went 18-12 with an RPI of 64.

Duke.summary: Duke returns 12 players and five of six starters off a 5-26 season, with 84% of its production coming back — the lone hole is middle blocker Ngozi Iloh, who started 30 matches and led the team with 246.0 points in 2025. Both top scorers are back in outside hitters Ashby Zubchevich (3.706 points per set) and Taylor Williams (3.527), and the middle rotation of Zoë Gillen-Malveaux and Breonna Goss also returns. The other two departures, setter Millie Muir and defensive specialist Christina Barrow, combined for little offensive volume. The ACC team finished 225th in our final 2025 rank and 260th in RPI, so continuity alone will have to do a lot of work.

Duquesne.summary: Emersen Schrom returns as the offense's clear focal point at 5.037 points per set, and she is not alone: the top six scorers are all back, including Karli Jordan (2.52) and Jordan Robertson (2.404). The losses are real but narrow — OH Carsyn Henschen (341.5 points) and MB Ariel Helm (320.0) both started all 31 matches, leaving two holes in the starting six with four starters returning. Overall, 64 percent of production comes back from an 18-13 season in the Atlantic 10, with just one transfer in to fill the gaps.

ETSU.summary: Makayla Bays carried this offense to an extreme degree, scoring 4.482 points per set as an outside hitter while no other returner cleared 2.0; she started all 29 matches and earned AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025. The middle is where the 23-7 season gets rebuilt, with Whitley Rammel (339.5 points) and Brianna Cantrell (311.0) both gone along with opposite Isabelle Iosua (234.5), leaving three of six starting spots open. Ten players return and 54 percent of production comes back, but the replacement pool is thin: one transfer in and five newcomers with no Division I record. The SoCon side finished 76th in final RPI after taking its bid through the conference tournament.

East Carolina.summary: East Carolina brings back five of six starters and 76% of its production from a 12-15 season, with the top five scorers all returning, led by outside hitter Ellie Pate at 3.912 points per set. The one hole is at middle blocker, where Carlia Northcross departs after 222.0 points and 26 starts. The rest of the departures are small — Violet Hakan (76.0 points) and Teegan Charapata (49.5) — and the roster adds one transfer in an American Conference team that finished 172nd in RPI.

East Texas A&M.summary: East Texas A&M ran a 5-1 in 2025 and leaned on a fixed core: Brooke Box (MB), Gracie Campbell (OH) and setter Haley Mullaney each started all 28 matches, with Nevaeh Smith starting 26 and Rendi Fetty 21. That continuity produced a 9-19 record and a Southland tournament bid, finishing 266th in our final rank and 251st in RPI. The lineup was known in 28 matches, though rotation sets agreed in only 24 of 156 resolved. No roster is posted for 2026, so none of the 2025 starters are confirmed back.

Eastern Ill..summary: A 24-8 season and an OVC tournament bid came with an unusually steep bill: eight players departed, including OH Destiny Walker (499.0 points, off to Virginia Tech), OH Lilli Amettis (313.0) and MB Emma Schroeder (248.5), leaving four of six starting spots open and just 29 percent of production returning. The two starters who stay are the right ones to keep — OH Katie Kopshever at 3.468 points per set and MB Anaya Rawlinson at 1.417, with Rawlinson having started 30 matches. Replacing the setter is the immediate problem, since Catalina Rochaix started 29 matches in the 5-1 and only two transfers came in against six newcomers with no DI record. The team finished 108 in RPI.

Eastern Ky..summary: Eastern Ky. keeps its two biggest offensive pieces — outside Addison Burke at 3.752 points per set and setter Emilee Hill, an AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025, at 3.12 — but has to rebuild around them, with three of six starting spots open. The departures are substantial: OH AG Hynes (372.5 points in 2025), MB Carson Ledford (305.5) and OH Amanda Mack (217.5, now at Holy Cross). Ten players return for 55% of production, joined by three transfers in a 5-1 that produced a 22-9 record and a UAC tournament bid. The final RPI landed at 70.

Eastern Mich..summary: Eastern Mich. is essentially rebuilding from scratch: 14 players departed and only 4 return, leaving 25% of production and just 1 of six starters back with 5 starting-six vacancies. The two biggest losses are OH Ava Siefke (456.5 points in 2025, off to Toledo) and MB Hatteras Welker (373.0 points, to Coastal Carolina), both of whom started all 31 matches. The returning core is thin but real at the pins, with AshleeKay Christensen at 2.683 points per set and Taeley Mahler at 2.134, and the roster adds 3 transfers alongside 10 newcomers with no DI record. The 5-1 offense went 13-18 last year with a final RPI of 247.

Eastern Wash..summary: Eastern Wash. keeps its scoring core intact after a 3-25 season: the top six point producers all return, led by outside hitter Kalista Lukovich at 3.636 points per set and Quincy Moran at 2.741. The losses are concentrated in setter Anna Bolich, who started 27 matches, and middle blocker Quincey McCoy, leaving three of six starting spots open. Returning production sits at 68 percent, with nine players back and no transfers added, so the five newcomers without a Division I record will have to fill the gaps in the 5-1.

Elon.summary: All six of the top scorers are back, led by outside hitter Anna Sewell at 2.914 points per set and Cameron Lanier at 2.614, with middle Catherine Rucker at 2.211. The losses are concentrated on the pin: Simrin Carlsen (249.5 points in 2025) and Clara Simmons (216.5) both started regularly and are gone, leaving two vacancies in the starting six and 52 percent of production returning. With no transfers in and four newcomers without a Division I record, the 5-1 will have to be rebuilt around holdovers after a 7-20 season in the CAA.

Evansville.summary: All six of the top per-set scorers are back, led by middle blocker Chloe Cline at 2.288 points per set and outside hitter Ryan Scheu at 2.254, which is unusual for a 6-22 team. The losses are concentrated elsewhere: Hinsley Everett (299.5 points in 2025), Josdarilee Caraballo (143.0) and setter Kora Ruff (42.0) all depart, leaving three of six starting spots open even with 66% of production returning. The setter vacancy matters most in a 5-1, and the incoming class offers little proven help with one transfer in and four newcomers without a DI record. Evansville finished 281st in our final rank and 283rd in RPI out of the MVC.

FDU.summary: FDU lost its entire outside hitter corps from an 18-12 season, with Kylie Nott (324.0 points), Giorgia Vaschetti (248.5) and Avery Bain (228.0) all gone, leaving four holes in the starting six and only 35% of production returning. What is back is the middle and the setter: Alessia Zampieri (2.265 points per set) and Angela Marchetto (1.604) return alongside setter Isabella Scarfone, who started 26 matches. Ava Deguzman, the top scorer at 2.353 points per set, also returns and becomes the obvious focal point on the pin. The replacement pool is thin — one transfer in and four newcomers with no Division I record — for a team that finished 255th in RPI.

FGCU.summary: All six of the top scorers from last season are listed as returning, led by outside hitter Julija Grubisic Cabo at 3.483 points per set and Katie Gielas at 2.935, with middle Abby Toeniskoetter at 2.507. The offsetting loss is outside hitter Barbara Koehler, whose 373.0 points in 2025 dwarf the next departures, Ava Smith at 184.0 and Iyanna Battle at 95.5. Roster churn is real — 10 players departed against 8 returning, two transfers in and three newcomers with no Division I record — but returning production still sits at 59 percent. The 19-9 season produced an ASUN bid via the conference tournament, a final RPI of 69 and a final ranking of 88.

FIU.summary: FIU is essentially starting over after a 20-12 season: 13 players departed, only 2 return, and returning production sits at 16 percent. Five of the six starting spots are open, with outside hitter Jillian Huckabey (27 matches started, 2.752 points per set) the lone returning starter. The losses include Kira Givans (437.0 points) and Rebekah Pfefferkorn (294.5), both outside hitters, plus middle Magda Stambrowska (237.5). The rebuild leans on 5 transfers in and 8 newcomers with no Division I record, in a group that finished 81st in RPI and reached the field via the CUSA tournament.

Fairfield.summary: Fairfield returns its top five scorers by points per set — led by Mamie Krubally at 3.306 and Emma Bortolotti at 2.631 — yet still has three of six starting spots to fill, including setter Abby Jandro, who started 28 matches. The departures of Allie Elliott (346.5 points) and Maya Walker (292.5) take away the two highest-volume pieces from a 25-6 season that ended with a MAAC tournament bid. Returning production sits at 64 percent with 12 players back, five gone, and no transfers in, so the seven newcomers without a DI record will decide how the 5-1 is staffed. The final RPI of 104 sat ahead of the No. 134 ranking.

Fla. Atlantic.summary: The top three scorers all return: Olivia Hart at 4.226 points per set, Anna Hartman at 3.0 and Libby Ashline at 2.601, which is the core of 70% returning production off a 19-11 season. The losses are concentrated on the pins and at setter, with Kayla Richardson (228.5 points) and Erin Morrissey (186.0) gone and three of six starting spots open. Two transfers arrive, Brooke Crummel and Sequoia Layne, both of whom scored above 1.9 points per set. The American entrant finished 79th in RPI after taking the conference tournament bid.

Florida.summary: Half the front-line scoring here is imported: three of the top six scorers by points per set are transfers, led by opposite Logan King at 4.18 and outside Kamryn Chaney at 4.008, part of 7 players brought in. Jordyn Byrd returns as the leading scorer at 4.276 points per set, though she started only 16 matches. The bigger problem is the middle and the setter spot — Jaela Auguste (378.5 points in 2025) left for Wisconsin and Alexis Stucky went to Penn St., leaving 3 starting-six vacancies from a 16-12 season that ended with a conference tournament bid. Returning production sits at 71 percent with 10 players back.

Florida A&M.summary: Almost everything comes back: 88% of production and five of six starters, with 13 players returning against 3 departures. The top six scorers are all returning, led by LaDonna Trantham (3.323 points per set), Farah Farooq (3.091) and Sydney Whitfield (3.045), so the only real hole in the 5-1 is outside hitter Yaricel Rodrigeuz, who accounted for 174.0 points in 2025. The results haven't matched the continuity yet — 14-17 with an RPI of 272 — and the two incoming transfers have no DI record.

Florida St..summary: All six of the top scorers are back, led by outside hitter Kyleene Filimaua at 4.35 points per set and middles Nenu Kpea (2.235) and Delaney Ewing (1.851), which is the core of 70% returning production. The losses are concentrated in two spots: setter Lily Nicholson, who started 24 matches and left for Texas A&M, and outside hitter Iane Henke, who put up 487 points and started 23. That leaves two vacancies in the starting six from a 16-13 season in the ACC, with three transfers in to help fill the 5-1.

Fordham.summary: Every one of the top six scorers from the 2025 season is back, led by outside hitter Erynn Sweeney at 2.858 points per set and Mila Micunovic at 2.539. The departures are concentrated in the pin: Audrey Brown (340.5 points) started all 28 matches and Zoe Talabong (228.5) started 21, leaving two holes in a starting six that otherwise returns four players, including setter Whitney Woodrow, who ran the 5-1 in all 28 matches. Returning production sits at 63 percent with no transfers in and four newcomers who have no Division I record, so the rebuild of the outside rotation is internal. The 9-19 finish left them 256th in the final RPI.

Fresno St..summary: Fresno St. brings back five of its six starters and all six of its top scorers, with only middle blocker Addison Haluska's 483 points from 2025 to replace. Jenna Legault, who started all 28 matches at outside hitter, led the team at 3.675 points per set, more than double the next scorer, Brooklyn Washington at 1.766. Returning production sits at 60 percent off a 7-22 season in the Pac-12, run out of a 5-1. Seven players departed and two transfers came in, three of the newcomers without a Division I record.

Furman.summary: All six starters are back for Furman, and 93 percent of production returns from a 21-9 season that ended with a SoCon tournament bid. The top six scorers are all returning, led by middle blocker Tennyson Gorman at 3.387 points per set with 27 starts, alongside outside hitters Lauren Haynes (2.986) and Ashley Stein (2.972). The main subtraction is middle blocker Grainne McGrath and her 92.0 points; only three players departed and no transfers came in, so continuity in the 5-1 is essentially total. That group finished 149th in RPI and 164th in our final rank.

Ga. Southern.summary: Georgia Southern ran a 5-1 in 2025 and rode a settled lineup: Kirsten Barrett, Reagan Barth and Sam Bowron each started all 28 matches, with Lydia Seymour at 27 and Alex Myers at 26. That group went 19-9 and took the Sun Belt's bid through the conference tournament, finishing 98th in our final rank against an RPI of 124. The serve order ran Myers, Mayte Camacho, Bowron, Maddie Cugino, Barrett, Barth, though the rotation data is only partly settled — 71 of 131 resolved sets agree.

Gardner-Webb.summary: Gardner-Webb brings back its entire top-six scoring group, led by Nicole Osborne (2.674 points per set) and Haedyn Crumbley (2.665), with Milla Lugo, Alexis Maesch, Samia Sayd and Caroline Franklin all returning as well. Overall returning production sits at 78 percent, with 15 players back and four of six starters, the holes being setter Sloane Rooney and middle Brookelyn Nance. The biggest departure by 2025 points is outside hitter Serena Kohler at 206. The 2025 season ended 11-19 out of the Big South, with a final RPI of 278.

George Mason.summary: George Mason ran a 5-1 in 2025 and reached the Atlantic 10 bid through the conference tournament, finishing 17-13. Middle blocker Meredith Brown started all 30 matches, with Avery Booker and Chelsea Colter at 27 apiece and Ava Cheney, Kiera Hamilton and Nia Thompson each at 24. The lineup data is thin in places: of 147 rotation sets resolved, only 42 agreed, across 30 matches with a known lineup. The team closed at No. 146 in RPI and No. 158 in our final rank, and no 2026 roster is posted yet for any of the listed starters.

George Washington.summary: George Washington went 19-12 in 2025 and reached the NCAA field through the Atlantic 10 tournament rather than at-large, finishing 132nd in RPI and 140th in our final rank. The 5-1 offense ran through setter Abby Markworth, who started 24 matches, with middle Sydney Hasenfratz (29 starts) and outside Alexis Rodriguez (28) the most constant presences in a lineup that leaned heavily on outside hitters. Rotation data is thin: of 131 resolved rotation sets across 30 matches with a known lineup, only 20 agreed. No 2026 roster is posted yet, so returners, departures and transfers are all unknown rather than zero.

Georgetown.summary: Georgetown brings back all six starters and 13 players in total, with 98% of its returning production intact after a 14-15 season. The only meaningful departure is middle blocker Vaughan Anoa'i, who scored 25.5 points in 2025; libero/DS Jade Smith adds another 5.0. The top six scorers, led by outside hitters Dionna Mitchell (3.339 points per set) and Samantha Soderlund (3.061), are all returning to the 5-1 offense. The Hoyas finished 131st in RPI and reached the field via the conference tournament out of the Big East.

Georgia.summary: Bianna Muoneke carried this offense, scoring 4.495 points per set as an outside hitter and earning AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025, and she is back. The SEC side went 16-10 out of a 5-1 system and keeps four of six starters, with 54 percent of its production returning; the holes are at middle blocker and the second outside spot, where MK Patten (274.5 points) and Estelle Haugen (191.5) departed. Setter Chloe Elarton returns after 23 starts, so the distribution should be settled, but only one transfer arrived to fill two vacancies in the starting six.

Georgia St..summary: An 18-10 season that produced a Sun Belt tournament bid has been almost entirely dismantled: 16 players departed, only 3 return, and just 22% of production comes back. Five of the six starting spots are open, with setter Shanelle Martinez (15 starts) and outside hitters Alessia Cappai (249.0 points) and Nazli Guvener (226.5) all gone; middle Akira Burt, who led the team at 2.846 points per set, is the lone returning starter. The rebuild leans on 5 transfers in and 8 newcomers with no Division I record, which makes the 5-1 system from last year no guarantee going forward.

Georgia Tech.summary: Georgia Tech loses its entire starting six on paper, with 3 starting-six vacancies and 0 starters returning, including OH Lameen Mambu (345.0 points in 2025) to Purdue and OH Noemi Despaigne (266.0) to Houston, plus MB DeAndra Pierce (232.5). The rebuild comes without help from the portal: 0 transfers in and 7 newcomers with no DI record, leaving returning production at 46 percent. What does come back is scoring — Anna Fiedorowicz (3.569 points per set), Larissa Mendes (3.083) and Bianca Garibaldi (2.953) are all listed as returning from a 16-14 team that finished 48th in RPI.

Gonzaga.summary: Gonzaga has four of six starting spots to fill after losing Sjakkie Donkers (477.0 points in 2025), Autumn Larson (229.5) and Fallon Thompson (228.5), leaving just 2 returning starters and 35% of its production. What's back is concentrated in the middle and on the pins: Taylor Walsh started all 29 matches at MB and scored 2.116 points per set, with Raechelle Dykstra at 2.077 and Dani Johnson at 1.665. The lone transfer in, Claire Wagstaff, was the top scorer on the list at 2.247 points per set, and 7 newcomers have no DI record. The 14-15 season ended with a final RPI of 207.

Grambling.summary: Grambling brings back 70% of its production and four of six starters after a 7-19 season, with two spots in the starting six open. The frontline loss is real: middle blocker Ra'Niya Brown accounted for 163.5 points in 2025, and fellow middle Morgan Munro (70.5) and outside Denver Watkins (56.5) also departed. Outside hitter Kenya Lucas returns as the leading scorer at 2.994 points per set, with Rihianna Brown (2.09) back in the middle, and transfer Lyric Jordan arrives at 2.807. The lineup picture is thin, though — only 4 matches had a known lineup, and just 14 of 105 resolved rotation sets agreed.

Grand Canyon.summary: Five of six starters are back for Grand Canyon, with the lone vacancy coming from outside hitter Anaelena Ramirez, who started all 30 matches and led the team with 422.5 points. The two projected top scorers are both transfers: Katie Schulz at 3.72 points per set and Starr Williams at 3.446, ahead of returning setter Bella Nunez at 2.832. Returning production sits at 56 percent, and the incoming class includes seven players with no Division I record alongside two transfers. The 2025 season ended 17-13 with an RPI of 87 and a conference tournament bid in the Mountain West.

Green Bay.summary: Green Bay brings back five of six starters and 70% of its production from an 11-19 season, with the top six scorers all returning, led by middle Diane Pichelman at 3.73 points per set and outside Gillian Koning at 3.136. The one hole is setter Emma Johnson, who started all 30 matches in the 5-1 and accounted for 101.5 points, and there are no transfers in to replace her — the seven newcomers have no DI record. Libero Katie Schulz, the biggest departure at 346 points, left for Grand Canyon, so the back row will also look different. The team finished 239th in our final rank and 253rd in RPI.

Hampton.summary: Hampton went 1-26 in 2025 yet brings back 75% of its production, including four of six starters in the 5-1. The two vacancies are middle Kylah McNeal, who led the team with 88.0 points, and setter Morgan Warren at 38.5, so the setting job is open. Racquel Frazier (2.948 points per set) and Katerina Pappa (2.727) both return on the outside, and one transfer joins three newcomers with no Division I record.

Harvard.summary: Harvard's top five scorers by points per set all return, led by outside hitter Sofia Rossi at 3.635 and middle Ryleigh Patterson at 2.981, which is the main reason 66% of production is back despite a 7-15 season. The losses are concentrated at the top of the pin rotation: Brynne Faltinsky (243.5 points) and Taylor Larkin (132.0) each started all 22 matches and are gone, leaving two holes in the starting six. There are no incoming transfers, so the 5-1 run by returning setter Sophia Wei will have to be filled from inside the roster of 10 returners.

Hawaii.summary: Hawaii returns its setter and three of six starters, with Adrianna Arquette and Miliana Sylvester each starting 29 matches in the 5-1 and Cha'lei Reid leading the team at 4.18 points per set. High Point.summary: High Point's scoring runs through the middle: Maya Bukovcan (2.933 points per set) and Addison Freeland (2.861) both return, and both started all 28 matches in the 5-1. The losses are concentrated at outside hitter, where Élodie Lalonde (350.5 points in 2025) and Gia Padilla (148.5) depart, leaving 2 vacancies in the starting six with 4 starters back. Hofstra.summary: A 22-4 season that ended with a CAA tournament bid leaves this roster largely rebuilt: only 1 of six starters returns, creating 5 vacancies in the starting lineup, with 8 players departed against 7 returning and no transfers in. The losses are concentrated at outside hitter, where Izadora Stedile (398.5 points) and Clara Bal (249.0) are both gone, along with setter Nina Jioshvili-Ravva (110.0), who left for South Fla. Returning production sits at 47 percent, and 6 newcomers have no Division I record.

Holy Cross.summary: Holy Cross brings back 15 players and 77% of its production from a 9-23 season, including four of six starters. The two holes are at setter and outside: Katie Russell (27 starts) and Taliah Lee, whose 338 points led the team before she transferred to Weber St. Emma Sorensen returns as the top scorer at 3.45 points per set, with a middle group of Kyla Harris, Lacey Murphy and Isa Glover all back. Houston.summary: Five of the six starting spots are open after 11 players departed, leaving just one returning starter and 21% of production back. Alyssa Gonzales, who started 22 matches at outside hitter, is the lone holdover among that group at 2.694 points per set. Houston finished 9-20 last season with an RPI of 163.

IU Indy.summary: IU Indy returns five of six starters and 79% of its production from an 18-14 season, with the only hole at middle blocker after Morgan Ostrowski, a 32-match starter who scored 406 points, departed. All six of the top scorers are back, led by opposite Jillian Tippmann at 3.909 points per set and outside hitter Maia Long at 2.684, behind returning setter Grace Purichia in the 5-1. The roster churn is minimal: four players left, one transfer arrived, and four newcomers have no Division I record. The Horizon side earned its bid through the conference tournament and finished 196th in our final rank, 208th in RPI.

Idaho.summary: Idaho brings back its top three scorers — Kiana Greer at 3.574 points per set, Sarah Sullivan at 1.969 and Koen Makaula at 1.958 — which is unusual for a 6-22 team. The losses are concentrated elsewhere: outside hitter Cayton White (331.0 points in 2025) and middle Gabrielle Smith (158.5) are gone, leaving two holes in the starting six with four starters back. Overall returning production sits at 52 percent, with eight players departed, six returning and two transfers in. The Big Sky finish left them 325th in final RPI.

Idaho St..summary: Idaho St. brings back its top four scorers by points per set, led by middle Jaydin Watts at 2.968 and outside Abby McClain at 2.741, with 61 percent of production returning from a 13-18 season. The losses are concentrated in two spots: middle Marci Bell (354.0 points) and opposite Meline Shulikov (229.0), leaving two vacancies in the starting six and four starters back. Setter Nora Waddoups returns after 26 starts, so the distribution should carry over. The Big Sky side finished 226th in final RPI, and its only path to the tournament is the conference tournament bid.

Illinois.summary: Illinois has to replace three of its six starters, including outside hitter Taylor de Boer (385.0 points in 2025) and opposite Auburn Tomkinson (276.5 points, now at UC Santa Barbara). What comes back is the top of the scoring chart: OH Alyssa Aguayo at 3.189 points per set and MB Ashlyn Philpot at 2.646, plus setter Kenna Phelan in the 5-1. Three transfers arrive, led by OPP Paityn Chapman (2.657 points per set) and MB Lindsay Oldendorf (2.094), with returning production at 47 percent. The 2025 season ended 13-16 with an RPI of 60.

Illinois St..summary: Illinois St. has to rebuild the middle and the pins at once: four of the six 2025 starting spots are vacant, with only two starters back and 39% of production returning. The departures are concentrated at the top of the scoring sheet — MB Khenedi Guest (301.0 points, now at Temple), MB Hannah Reichensperger (262.5) and OH Aida Shadewald (254.0) are all gone. The replacements are largely imported: four transfers in and five newcomers with no Division I record, with transfer OH Emilija Arsic (2.419 points per set) projected ahead of returning OPP Ruth Ziegler (2.398). The top four scorers all return, led by outside hitter Jaidyn Jager at 3.965 points per set and middle Ella Boersema at 2.655, but the roster still loses its two biggest offensive pieces in Candela Alonso-Corcelles (465.0 points) and Avry Tatum (405.5). That leaves three of six starting spots open and 46 percent of production returning, with no transfers added to fill them.

Indiana St..summary: Indiana St. brings back 14 players and 84% of its production after a 9-19 season, with five of six starters returning and only one vacancy in the starting six. The lone significant departure is middle blocker Kimora Whetstone, who started all 27 matches and scored 198.5 points. The top six scorers are all back, led by outside hitters Kira Holland (3.877 points per set) and Ava Robart (3.041). There were no transfers in, so the MVC club is relying entirely on internal development to replace Whetstone in the middle.

Iona.summary: Almost everything comes back from an 11-21 season: 14 players returning, 86% of production, and five of six starters, with the top six scorers all listed as returning. The one hole is at setter, where Caleigh Schroeder started 31 matches in the 5-1 and departs alongside OH Taylor Timko, who left for Mercer. Julia Leonardo is the clear first option at 4.014 points per set, well ahead of Gabby Taylor at 2.435. With no transfers in and five newcomers who have no Division I record, the fix at setter has to come from inside the room.

Iowa.summary: Iowa has to rebuild four of six starting spots, including the entire setting position after Claire Ammeraal started all 32 matches and departed. The 5-1 offense also loses its top two scorers by total points, Chard'e Vanzandt (438.5) and Alyssa Worden (243.0), leaving 42 percent of production returning. What comes back is the front-row scoring core: Carmel Vares at 2.821 points per set and Hannah Whittingstall at 2.684, both returning from a 15-17 season. Two transfers arrive, and neither is without a Division I record.

James Madison.summary: All six starters return from a 22-9 season, with 96% of production coming back and zero vacancies in the starting lineup. The main hole is setter Rebecca Watkins, who accounted for 56.0 points and ran the 5-1; Grace Wenrich, who started 28 matches, is the setter still on hand. Four of six starters are back but returning production sits at 44 percent, and only two transfers arrived against eight departures. The Big 12 regular-season champion finished 14th in RPI.

Kansas City.summary: Kansas City returns its top four scorers by points per set — Ryanne Wattree (2.317), Emry Brown (2.287), Mia Weaver (1.847) and Stella Smith (1.667) — yet lost Ledisi Kpea, an outside hitter who led the team with 260.5 points in 2025 and transferred to UTSA. Eight players left and three transfers arrived, with five newcomers who have no Division I record. Kennesaw St..summary: Kennesaw St. is built around its middles: Olivia Burrage (3.044 points per set), Haley Patterson (2.417) and Maggie Byrd (1.511) all return after a 19-9 season and a CUSA tournament bid. Kent St..summary: Kent St. brings back five of six starters from an 8-21 season, including setter Christina Vigil, who started all 27 matches in the 5-1 offense, and middles Nadia Miller (2.848 points per set) and Adalynn Ginley (2.321). The lone hole is at outside, where Mackenzie McGuire departs after 402 points. Returning production sits at 69 percent, and three transfers arrive, among them Vanessa Imoh at 2.133 points per set. Kentucky.summary: Kentucky returns five of six starters from a 30-3 season, including AVCA First Team pick Brooklyn DeLeye (5.06 points per set) and Freshman of the Year setter Kassie O'Brien, who ran the 5-1 in 30 starts. Setter Delfina Schuh returns after starting 26 matches in the 5-1.

Liberty.summary: Liberty brings back 87% of its production and five of six starters from a 20-10 season, including the entire top scoring group: outside hitters Paige Overcash (3.61 points per set), Carly O'Brien (3.538) and Jenna Otts (3.403). Lindenwood.summary: Lindenwood brings back 87% of its production and all four of its leading scorers, headlined by outside hitter Autumn Bax at 3.745 points per set and middle Ashley Geluck at 3.186. Four of six starters return, leaving two openings in the starting lineup, with middle Faith Atkins (114.5 points in 2025) the largest departure along with both setters who started, Amelia Thro and Meghan Donoughue. The 5-1 offense went 11-16 last season and finished 270th in RPI. Reinforcements are thin: one transfer in and two newcomers without a Division I record.

Lipscomb.summary: Lipscomb's top five scorers by points per set all return, led by outside hitter Ella Durham at 3.073 and middle Brooklyn Fuchs at 2.019, yet returning production still sits at 43 percent because the departures were concentrated in the starting lineup. Three of six starters are back, leaving three vacancies, including both halves of the 6-2 setter tandem's Sophia Hudepohl side and outside Courtney Jones, who led the team with 392 points in 2025. There are no incoming transfers and four newcomers without a Division I record, so the replacements come from inside the program. Little Rock.summary: Little Rock returns just one of its six primary starters and 29% of its production, with nine players gone and five of the starting six spots open. Outside hitter Bella Cherry is the one anchor, starting all 31 matches and leading the team at 3.597 points per set. The rebuild is being handled with one transfer in and five newcomers without a Division I record, after a 16-15 season that ended with an RPI of 212.

Long Beach St..summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after a 22-9 season, with only 31% of production returning and just two starters back. The exits are heavy at the top: opposite Logan King (476.5 points, now at Florida), outside Elise Agi (375.0) and middle Rhiann Sheffie (266.0) all leave from a 5-1 that started the same core nearly every match. Sidney Hamaker, who led the team at 2.56 points per set while starting 15 matches, and setter Madi Maxwell (1.693) are the pieces to build around, alongside four transfers in and four newcomers with no Division I record. The bid came through the Big West tournament, with a final RPI of 77.

Louisiana.summary: Louisiana returns four of six starters from a 15-11 season, including outside hitters Grace Sweeney (2.72 points per set) and Marlee Ervin (2.689), plus middle Lindsey Henry and setter Ryleigh Garis in the 5-1. The holes are at opposite and middle, where Cailin Demps (241.5 points) and Chelsea Gilmore (146.0) departed, part of a group that leaves returning production at 41 percent. Incoming transfer Taylor Gaines led the scoring list at 2.892 points per set, which would replace much of that. The Sun Belt team finished 142nd in our final rank and 144th in RPI.

Louisiana Tech.summary: The top four scorers by points per set all return, led by Gabrielle Hairston at 2.027 and Zari Gillispie at 2.02, yet the outside hitter group was gutted: Jailen Hurley (263.0 points), Giulia Bonifacio (215.5) and Grace Luevanos (143.0) are all gone. That leaves three of six starters back and three vacancies in the starting lineup, with returning production at 43 percent. There are no incoming transfers and six newcomers with no Division I record, so the rebuild runs through setter Sydnee Carter, who started all 26 matches in the 5-1. The 9-21 season finished 277th in RPI.

Louisville.summary: Five of six starters are back from a 26-7 season, including setter Nayelis Cabello and the two outsides who carried the offense: Payton Petersen at 3.607 points per set and Chloe Chicoine at 3.601. The one hole is at middle, where Cara Cresse started all 33 matches and scored 414.5 points before departing. Cabello and Chicoine both took AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025, and 78 percent of production returns to the 5-1. The ACC regular-season champion finished 12th in final RPI.

Loyola Chicago.summary: The middle blocker spot is where Loyola Chicago's offseason bill comes due: Ann Marie Remmes started all 32 matches and led the team with 409.5 points in 2025, and fellow MB Karli Molnau (273.5 points) left for Bowling Green. Avary DeBlieck, who started 30 matches in the middle, is the one holdover at the position. The 17-16 finish came with an RPI of 114 in the Atlantic 10, and two transfers plus three newcomers with no DI record arrive to fill two starting-six vacancies.

Loyola Maryland.summary: All six of Loyola Maryland's top scorers are back, led by outside hitter Ava Nepkin at 2.806 points per set and Morgan Crawford at 2.211, which is why returning production sits at 65 percent. Gabi Verdicchio, who started 18 matches in the 6-2, is the obvious internal answer at setter. The 7-18 record and No. 280 RPI finish set a low bar in the Patriot League, where the bid comes from the conference tournament.

Manhattan.summary: Manhattan brings back five of six starters and 75% of its production after a 4-23 season, with the top six scorers all returning except outside hitter Fiona VanDyke, who left for Central Ark. after 317 points. Hanna Kaczynska leads that group at 3.578 points per set, followed by Emma Francesconi at 2.219 and Katie Powers at 2.218, giving the 5-1 offense a settled outside rotation. There were no transfers in and six newcomers with no DI record, so the one open spot in the starting six will be filled from inside the program. The MAAC side finished 335th in our final rank and 340th in RPI.

Marist.summary: Nearly everything comes back here: 14 players returning, 5 of the six starters, and 90% of returning production after a 10-20 season. The one clear hole is setter, where Claire Lewis started 18 matches and departed, and there are no transfers in — 0 — to replace her, leaving 3 newcomers with no DI record. The MAAC team finished 317th in our final rank and 307th in RPI.

The departures include the whole outside hitter group and the setter: Natalie Ring (557.5 points in 2025, now at Texas A&M), Hattie Bray (384.0) and Elena Radeff (264.0), all of whom started at least 26 matches. The rebuild leans on two transfers, with Carson Tyler (4.802 points per set) and Lauren Young (1.739) arriving to join returners Emma Parks (1.968) and Schmidt (1.4). The Big East team went 18-11 last season and finished 32nd in RPI after taking the conference tournament bid.

Marshall.summary: Marshall keeps its top five scorers from a 15-15 season, headlined by outside hitter Emma Barnett at 3.491 points per set and middle Beatrice Ciccarelli at 3.088, and returns 75% of its production. The losses are concentrated: opposite Elli Barry (187.0 points) and outside Audrey Geer (143.5, now at Ball St.) are gone along with setter Bella Thompson, leaving three of six starting spots open despite the returning firepower. Replacing Thompson matters most in a 5-1, and the staff brought in four transfers plus three newcomers with no Division I record. The Sun Belt team finished 181st in our final rank and 166th in RPI.

Maryland.summary: Maryland brings back its top four scorers, led by outside hitter Haley Melby at 2.439 points per set and middle Eva Rohrbach at 2.232, with 52 percent of production returning after an 8-22 season. The holes are at the pins and in the setting spot: Ajack Malual (457.5 points in 2025) and setter Lilly Wagner, who went to Stanford, both departed, leaving four of six starters back and two vacancies in the starting lineup. Only one transfer arrived against six departures, so the 5-1 run last year will need a new setter from within or from six newcomers with no Division I record.

No 2026 roster is available yet for any of the top starters, so returning personnel is unknown; the RPI finished 291st.

Memphis.summary: Memphis brings back its top two scorers, Amanda Hardt at 5.419 points per set and Zaniah Hoskins at 3.543, along with 72% of its production and four of six starters. The losses are concentrated in the middle and on the left: Brianna Washington (168.0 points in 2025) and Jasmyn Tate (135.5) are gone, leaving two holes in the starting six. An 11-20 record in the American came with a final RPI of 242, and the roster churn is modest — one transfer in and four newcomers with no Division I record. Setter is the question, with Sydney Marshall (16 starts) back in the 5-1 but Madelyn Bach (14 starts) departed.

Mercer.summary: Mercer's middle blockers are the backbone here: Avery Wilks and Joselynn Sanjurjo each started all 30 matches and both return, with Wilks scoring 2.383 points per set and Sanjurjo 1.684.
