There were no transfers in, so the six newcomers with no DI record are the only outside additions to a 5-1 offense. The final marks were 244th in our rank and 232nd in RPI.

Ole Miss.summary: Ole Miss loses its two highest-volume pieces from a 14-15 season: outside hitter Gabi Placide, who started all 29 matches and scored 558.5 points before transferring to SMU, and setter Mokihana Tufono, also a 29-match starter in the 5-1. Four of six starters return, leaving two vacancies, with 60% of production back and middles Tessa Jones, Keirstyn Carlton and Carly Paugh among them. The incoming answers are transfers: opposite Jorda Crook at 4.903 points per set and middle Nina Moorer at 2.837, alongside returning outside Shayla Meyer at 3.307. The SEC team finished 63rd in our final rank and 78th in RPI.

Omaha.summary: Omaha has to rebuild most of a starting lineup: four of six starting spots are vacant, with only two starters back and returning production at 38 percent. The departures are led by outside hitter Kali Jurgensmeier (423.5 points in 2025), plus middles Emily Huss (174.0) and Morgan DeBow (168.5). Faith Venable returns as the top scorer at 3.711 points per set after starting all 26 matches, and setter Julia Owens is back from 20 starts in the 5-1. The 2025 season ended 10-16 with an RPI of 219 in the Summit League.

Oral Roberts.summary: No 2026 roster information exists yet for Oral Roberts — all six of the most-used starters, from middle blocker Jenna Salyer's 28 starts down to libero Sophie Johnson's 15, are listed as not back, with zero returners, zero departures logged and zero transfers in. The 2025 season ended 3-25, with a final RPI of 320 and a rank of 318. The Summit League team's path to a bid runs through the conference tournament. Lineup data is thin in places: of 125 resolved rotation sets across 28 matches with a known lineup, only 15 agreed.

Oregon.summary: Oregon keeps its top scorer, AVCA Third Team opposite Alanah Clemente, who put up 4.726 points per set in 2025, along with Valentina Vaulet at 3.918. The losses are heavy elsewhere: setter Cora Taylor and middle Iva Sucurovic both started all 29 matches and are gone, as is outside Sophia Meyers, the team's biggest points loss at 300.5. That leaves 3 of six starters back, 3 starting-six vacancies to fill, and 57 percent returning production from a 17-13 season that ended with a conference tournament bid. Four transfers in and four newcomers with no DI record have to cover the setter spot in a 5-1.

Oregon St..summary: Oregon St. is rebuilding most of its front line after a 19-9 season, with only 2 of six starters back and 28% of production returning. Lauren Rumel (424.5 points), Maeli Cormier (285.0) and Annika Hester (252.5) all departed, leaving four starting-six vacancies filled partly by four incoming transfers. The projected scoring leans on transfer OPP Taylor Treahy (3.39 points per set) and returning MB Alana Marrs (2.959), who started 27 matches. The team finished 107th in RPI and 76th in our final rank after taking its bid through the conference tournament.

Pacific.summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after an 8-21 season, with only setter Alessia Couchond back among last year's regular starters and returning production at 23 percent. The departures carry the offense with them: Olivia Keller (379.5 points), Logan Blutreich (206.0) and Valentina Varani (197.0) are all gone. The rebuild leans on three transfers in, including Nicole Zake at 3.646 points per set, alongside returning outside hitters Hannah Koester (2.141) and Mila Stojakovic (1.991). The WCC team finished 274th in our final 2025 rank and 303rd in RPI.

Penn.summary: All six starters are back for 2026, leaving zero vacancies in the starting lineup and 93% of production returning from a 12-12 season. The scoring load stays intact at the top: Zada Sanger (3.588 points per set), Ellie Siskin (3.089) and Jenna Garner (3.051) all return, as do middles Adell Murray (2.458) and Haley Kerstetter (2.432). The departures are all outside hitters, led by Jalen Tennyson's 53.5 points in 2025, and there are no transfers in, so continuity comes from the 13 returning players rather than additions. The Quakers ran a 5-1 and finished 227th in RPI, in a league where the bid is awarded by conference tournament.

Penn St..summary: Kennedy Martin returns after producing 6.222 points per set, more than double the next-closest scorer, Emmi Sellman at 2.437. The middle is the problem: Maggie Mendelson (285.0 points) and Jordan Hopp (191.0) both departed, along with setter Addie Lyon, leaving three of six starting spots open. Even so, 70 percent of production returns, with nine players back and three transfers in, including Whitney Lauenstein and Ryla Jones. The 19-13 record and No. 29 RPI came with a conference tournament bid out of the Big Ten.

Pepperdine.summary: Pepperdine brings back 84% of its production and 12 players, including four of six starters from a 21-8 season that ended with the WCC regular-season title and an at-large-free automatic bid. The middle-blocker duo of Ella Piskorz (3.316 points per set) and Irelynd Lorenzen (2.045) both return, as does outside hitter Chloe Pravednikov (3.189), and Piskorz, Pravednikov, Lorenzen and setter Tristen Raymond each started all 29 matches in the 5-1. The main hole is middle Vanessa Polk, who scored 241 points and started 25 matches before departing, one of two vacancies in the starting six. Roster churn is otherwise modest: one transfer in, seven newcomers with no DI record.

Pittsburgh.summary: Olivia Babcock returns after winning the 2025 AVCA Player of the Year award, and her 5.972 points per set dwarfs the next name on the list, Blaire Bayless at 2.908 — both are back. The bigger question is the middle and the setter spot: Bre Kelley (261.5 points) and Ryla Jones (157.5 points) are both gone at MB, as is 35-match starter Brooke Mosher at setter, leaving three of six starting spots vacant. A 30-5 record in the ACC and 68 percent returning production give the rebuild a solid base, with two transfers in to help fill it.

Portland.summary: Five of six starters return, including setter Havannah Hoeft and the entire middle pairing, leaving one vacancy in the starting lineup after a 14-15 season. The lone real hole is at outside hitter, where Lucia Busso (339.0 points) and Elin Larsson (331.5) both departed; Maui Robins, who led the team at 3.418 points per set, is back to anchor the pin. Returning production sits at 59 percent, and the one incoming transfer, Lillian Lansing, arrives having scored 2.111 points per set. The 5-1 offense stays in place, with the WCC's automatic bid going to the regular-season champion.

Portland St..summary: Alivia Eikenberg is the rare outside hitter who returns after leading the team at 4.188 points per set, and she anchors a group that keeps three of six starters, including setter Ava Blascziek in the 5-1. The departures are concentrated on the pins and in the middle: Tyra Schaub (305.0 points in 2025), Naomi White (263.0, now at Washington St.) and Sydney Stenson (190.5) all go, leaving three starting-six vacancies. Portland St. went 11-17 and finished 262nd in RPI, with 51 percent of its production returning and only two transfers in against six newcomers with no Division I record.

Prairie View.summary: Prairie View brings back 87% of its production, including its top four scorers by points per set: Kylee Owens (4.225), D'Mya Hill (3.415), Iyonna Sherwood (2.398) and Valencia Wilder (1.917). Four of six starters return, leaving two holes in the starting six — middle Adlene Jideofor, who led all departures with 146.0 points in 2025, and setter MaKinzie Taplin, which matters in a 5-1. Owens, an AVCA Honorable Mention in 2024, started all 29 matches. The 18-12 record came with a SWAC bid earned through the conference tournament, and the team finished 263rd in our final rank against an RPI of 252.

Presbyterian.summary: Presbyterian brings back five of its six starters and 77% of its production after a 6-20 season, including setter Anisa Dorlouis, who started all 24 matches in the 5-1. The top six scorers by points per set are all returning, led by outside hitter Julia Yurkovich at 3.005 and opposite Courtney Williams at 2.62. The one hole is at middle blocker, where Elyse Hutchinson and her team-leading 204.5 points departed. Seven newcomers arrive without a Division I record, alongside two transfers.

Princeton.summary: Princeton returns its top six scorers by points per set, including OH Erin McNair at 3.222 and RS Taylor Clarke at 2.5, and setter Sydney Draper, who ran the 5-1 and picked up AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025. The departures are concentrated in two starting spots: MB Lucia Scalamandre (315.0 points) and OH Valerie Nutakor (312.0), leaving 4 of six starters back and 58 percent of production. There are no transfers in, so the two vacancies fall to a returning group of 13 plus two newcomers with no DI record. The 18-7 season finished at 84 in RPI.

Providence.summary: Providence brings back five of six starters and 83% of its production from a 12-17 season, with the only hole at outside hitter after Audrey Kocon (261.5 points in 2025) left for St. Thomas (MN). Setter Miller McDonald and outside hitter Sophia Adkins each started all 29 matches, and Adkins led the team at 4.164 points per set in the 5-1. The rest of the scoring core returns as well, including Macy Taylor at 2.937 points per set and middles Lyric Berry and Tori Otter. Roster churn is minimal: four players departed, one transfer in, and five newcomers with no Division I record.

Purdue.summary: Three players earned AVCA honours in 2025 — Taylor Anderson and Kenna Wollard on the Second Team, Grace Heaney on the Third — and all three are back, along with 4 of the six starters and 72 percent of returning production. Wollard led the scoring at 4.863 points per set out of the 5-1, with Heaney at 3.656; both return. The losses are concentrated at outside and middle, with Akasha Anderson (398.5 points in 2025) and Lindsey Miller gone, leaving 2 vacancies in the starting six. A 27-7 record and a conference tournament bid put them 10th in final RPI.

Purdue Fort Wayne.summary: A 3-26 season returns almost intact: 10 players are back, five of the six primary starters return, and 87% of production comes back with zero transfers in. Riley Rosneck (4.271 points per set) and fellow outside Trinity Rye (2.867) both started all 29 matches, and middle Mya Plemons (2.481) is back as well. The one hole is at middle blocker, where Jena Medearis and her 190.5 points depart, leaving a single vacancy in the starting six. The 5-1 offense stays in the hands of returning setter Haiden Means.

Queens (NC).summary: Queens (NC) brings back five of six starters and 64% of its production from an 18-12 season, with the only real hole on the outside where Mia McMillen (284.5 points) departs. The returning scoring core is deep on the pins: Callie DeSchryver at 3.011 points per set, Emma Norris at 2.982 and Elizabeth Layson at 2.855, all back, along with setter Tyler Peluso, who started 16 matches in the 5-1. There are no transfers in, so the seven newcomers without a DI record are the only outside additions. The team finished 173rd in RPI after taking the ASUN's bid through the conference tournament.

Quinnipiac.summary: Quinnipiac went 19-12 in 2025 and reached the NCAA field through the MAAC conference tournament, despite finishing 218th in final RPI and 229th in our final ranking. The lineup data here is thin: only 1 match with a known lineup, and each of the six charted starters — Asia Belli, Damla Gunes, Elena Giacomini, Ginevra Giovagnoni, Leilani-kai Giusta and Milena Silva — is credited with 1 start. Rotation tracking resolved 146 sets with 46 in agreement. No 2026 roster is posted, so returning and departing player counts are unavailable.

Radford.summary: Radford returns its entire top six scorers by points per set, led by outside hitter Olivia Ryno at 2.684 and Aubrey Hatch at 2.29, which is unusual for a 10-20 team. The losses are concentrated at setter and in the middle: Rylee Sloss (227.5 points in 2025) went to Dayton, and with Sierra Moore and Alana Kolb also gone, three of six starting spots are open. Overall returning production sits at 63 percent, with nine players back and nine departed, one transfer in and five newcomers without a Division I record. The Big South team finished 258th in final RPI.

Rhode Island.summary: Rhode Island keeps a lot of a 5-25 team together: 11 players return, 68% of production comes back, and three of the six primary starters are back, including outside hitter Havyn Rolle, the leading scorer at 2.762 points per set. The losses are concentrated on the pins, with Emma Vente (221.0 points) and Aerin Bowman (217.5) both gone from the outside. The one addition is middle blocker Emily Sawyer, a transfer who scored 2.06 points per set, which matters with three starting-six spots open. The 2025 season ended at No. 300 in RPI out of the Atlantic 10, where the bid comes from the conference tournament.

Rice.summary: Rice returns its top three scorers by points per set — Aaliyah Smith at 2.908, Arissa Smith at 2.668 and Kellen Dorotik at 2.418 — and brings back 4 of six starters, with 52% of production returning. The losses are concentrated in two spots: OH Taylor Preston (511.5 points in 2025) and MB Lademi Ogunlana (265.0), both of whom started all 30 matches, leaving 2 vacancies in the starting six. Four transfers arrive, including OH Amalia Simmons at 2.517 points per set. The 21-10 season ended with an RPI of 28 and a bid via the conference tournament.

Rider.summary: The two holes to fill are both on the pin and in the middle: outside hitter Kiannisha Santiago, who started all 32 matches and led the team with 515.0 points, and middle blocker Carley McAleavey (278.5 points) are gone, leaving 2 starting-six vacancies. Everything else stays intact — 4 of six starters return, including setter Makenna Mason (31 starts) in the 5-1, along with 12 players overall and 47% of production. Rylah Robinson is the top returning scorer at 2.577 points per set, with Erynn Gotsch (2.307) and Molly Rohde (2.061) behind her, and one transfer arrives in Aubrey Baker at 2.439. The 16-16 record and 221 RPI finish reflect a MAAC team that goes as far as the conference tournament allows.

Robert Morris.summary: Robert Morris returns its entire top-six scoring group, led by Tia Schultz at 2.178 points per set and Layla Todd at 2.149, yet still has to replace three of six starters. The departures are the ones that hurt structurally: setter Kaitlyn Brown, who started all 28 matches in the 5-1, outside Jocelyn Jourdan (426.5 points in 2025, now at North Texas), and middle Azra Eric (232.5 points). Returning production sits at 48 percent after a 9-20 season, with one transfer in and three newcomers who have no Division I record. The rotation data is thin — only 40 of 144 resolved rotation sets agreed — so the lineup picture beyond the returning scorers is unsettled.

Rutgers.summary: Rutgers keeps its top scorer in outside hitter Aspen Maxwell, who put up 4.018 points per set while starting 31 matches, but has to rebuild half the front of its lineup: three of six starters return and three spots are open, with OH Lexi Visintine (309.0 points) and MB Zora Hardison (285.5 points, now at Michigan St.) both gone. Returning production sits at 51 percent, with 10 players back, 5 departed, and 3 transfers in, including outside hitter Skylar George at 3.422 points per set. The 2025 season ended 12-20 out of the Big Ten, with a final RPI of 179. The 5-1 offense ran across 32 matches with a known lineup.

SFA.summary: The top five returning scorers are all back, led by outside hitter Katherine Holtman at 3.41 points per set and Kennedy Jones at 2.84, yet three of the six starting spots are still open. The departures are heavy at the pins: Camryn Hill (329.0 points in 2025) and Ilana De Assis (269.0) both leave from the outside, along with middle Izabella Ortiz (139.5), and setter Jayden Flynn is gone from the 5-1. Returning production sits at 58 percent with seven players back and seven departed, and the incoming class is thin — one transfer in and four newcomers with no Division I record. The 23-8 season ended with a Southland tournament bid and an RPI of 66.

SIUE.summary: SIUE brings back its top six scorers, led by outside hitter Sophie Robinson at 3.396 points per set, with Kennedy Pike (2.332) and Teagan Sullivan (2.079) also returning on the pin. Four of six starters are back and returning production sits at 64 percent, though the departures of Kyndia Smith (284.5 points in 2025) and middle Grace Nichols (196.0) leave two holes in the starting six. The roster adds no transfers and four newcomers without a Division I record, so the 12-18 finish in the OVC will have to improve from inside the returning group.

SMU.summary: SMU won the ACC regular-season title at 27-6, then lost setter Averi Carlson and opposite Malaya Jones, who led the roster with 600.0 points, from a lineup that started all 33 matches. Four of six starters are back, including AVCA Honorable Mention picks Jadyn Livings and Favor Anyanwu, but returning production sits at 44 percent with two spots in the starting six open. The portal answer is two outside hitters, Gabi Placide at 5.124 points per set and Suli Davis at 4.971, both incoming transfers who would immediately outscore anyone returning.

Sacramento St..summary: Victoria Marthaler carried this offense, scoring 5.381 points per set as an outside hitter and earning AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025 — more than double the 2.461 of the next-highest returner, Keonahi'ilani Solaita. The 20-10 record and a conference tournament bid came out of the Big West with a 5-1 system, though the RPI finished 140th. Three of six starters are back, including Marthaler, but setter Kate Doorn and middle Ashlynn Archer, who led the departures with 396.5 points, both started all 29 matches. Returning production sits at 61 percent with three starting spots open and just one transfer in.

Sacred Heart.summary: The entire outside hitter core comes back: Ryleigh Short (3.724 points per set), Abbie Hagedorn (3.203) and Lauren Hubert (3.078) all started 30 matches and are returning, which is most of why returning production sits at 68 percent. The losses are concentrated in the middle and at setter — both middle blockers, Emily Sawyer (239.0 points) and Cristina Montanez (219.5), are gone, along with setter Ava Roodbol, leaving three vacancies in the starting six and one incoming transfer to help fill them. Sacred Heart went 11-19 last season and finished 292nd in RPI, reaching the NCAA field through the MAAC tournament. Rebuilding the middle and running the 5-1 with a new setter is the whole offseason.

Saint Francis.summary: A 5-1 offense built around remarkable lineup stability: five starters — setter Alexandra Sappia, outsides Alyssa Irwin, Kori McClure and Korrin Burns, and libero Chandler Alter — each started all 19 matches with a known lineup, with outside Hailey Atkins starting 17. That group went 20-9 and took the NEC's automatic bid through the conference tournament, finishing 214th in RPI and 250th in our final rank. The rotation data is only partly settled, with 64 of 148 resolved rotation sets in agreement, and no roster information is available for 2026.

Saint Louis.summary: Saint Louis brings back its entire top six scorers, headlined by outside hitter Ellie Rink at 3.74 points per set, with Tea Kalajdzic (2.764) and Tamia Maddox (2.711) also returning on the pins. Four of six starters are back, including setter Jetta Brenning, middle Kayla Jansen and Maddox, who each started all 28 matches in the 5-1, leaving two vacancies where Irmak Gokcen (190.5 points) and Kennedy Cooper (76.5, now at North Texas) departed. Returning production sits at 81 percent off a 13-16 season that finished 222nd in our rank and 217th in RPI. Two transfers and two newcomers with no DI record join nine returners.

Saint Mary's (CA).summary: Saint Mary's returns just one of six starters and 11% of its production, with 12 players gone and only 4 back after an 11-18 season. The departures are the entire top of the scoring sheet: Genevieve Bane (387.0 points), Mya Allen (278.0, to Alabama) and Tessa Schouten (236.5, to San Diego St.), leaving five vacancies in the starting six. Six transfers in fill most of that gap, and the projected point leaders are middles Maddie Way (1.887 points per set) and Ava Galvan (1.86), both newcomers, with returning MB Anaya Thrower (1.617) the one holdover who started regularly at 19 matches.

Saint Peter's.summary: Roster churn is the story here: 15 players departed and only 8 return, with no transfers in and 5 newcomers who have no Division I record. The biggest single loss is OH Sibana González Acevedo, who scored 297.5 points in 2025, well ahead of MB Elena Bilhartz at 167.5. What does come back is a scoring core, with Valeria Pagan Munoz (2.56 points per set), Karolina T. Rodriguez Mendez (2.522) and Indira T. Benitez Dumeng (2.473) all returning, leaving returning production at 45 percent. The 7-22 record and No. 338 final RPI set the baseline in the MAAC.

Sam Houston.summary: The top scorer is back: Chloe Monson put up 3.87 points per set as an outside hitter and returns, as does middle Chelsea Butler at 2.291. The losses are real, though — Lauren Malone (354.0 points in 2025) and Lillian Hamilton (197.5) both leave the outside, and the setter in this 5-1, Avery Fowler, departs after starting all 29 matches. That leaves three of six starting spots open and 56 percent of production returning, with one transfer in and five newcomers who have no Division I record. An 11-18 season in CUSA is the baseline the rebuilt lineup starts from.

Samford.summary: Ally Cordes carried this offense at 4.121 points per set, more than triple the next returner, middle Janie Stinchcomb at 1.27, and both are back. Almost everything else is gone: four of the six starting spots are open, nine players departed including OH Kaleigh Meritt (429.0 points, to Dayton), MB Greer Golden (233.5) and OPP Sydney Waller (167.0), leaving 37 percent of production returning. Samford went 13-15 in the SoCon last season, finishing 186th in RPI. The rebuild leans on one transfer in and seven newcomers with no Division I record, with the setter spot vacated after Shea Bruntmyer's 24 starts in the 5-1.

San Diego.summary: Nemo Beach is back after leading the team at 4.516 points per set and earning AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025, and setter Kylie Munday returns after 29 starts in the 5-1. Four of the six starters return, leaving two spots in the starting lineup open, with 54% of production coming back from a 25-5 season that produced the WCC regular-season champion's bid. The departures are concentrated on the pins and in the middle: Isabel Clark (435.0 points) and Kali Engeman (314.0 points) are both gone. Two transfers arrive, including outside hitter Kierstyn Barton at 3.996 points per set, alongside seven newcomers with no DI record.

San Diego St..summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after nine departures, including the top three scorers from a 15-16 season: Taylor Underwood (400 points), Madison Corf (256) and Campbell Hague (231), who started 28 matches at middle before leaving for Tulsa. Only two starters return, and returning production sits at 27 percent, with seven players back and four transfers in. The projected scoring load leans on newcomer Haylee Brown at 3.768 points per set, with returning outside Ella Schabort next at 2.311. The Pac-12 side finished 170th in RPI and 137th in our final 2025 rank.

San Francisco.summary: San Francisco is rebuilding almost from scratch: 13 players departed and only 3 return, leaving 1 of six starters back and 5 vacancies in the starting lineup, with returning production at 18 percent. The outside hitter room took the heaviest hit, as Astrid Puig (296.0 points) left for Pepperdine and Emilija Arsic (208.0) for Illinois St., both of whom started at least 23 matches. Middle blocker Maeve Bailey, who led the team at 2.461 points per set and started 21 matches, is the one returning starter. The incoming group is 3 transfers plus 7 newcomers with no Division I record, after a 7-21 season in the WCC.

San Jose St..summary: San Jose St. brings back 86% of its production and four of six starters from a 13-16 season, with no vacancies in the starting six. The top six scorers are all listed as returning, led by Lolohea Fonua at 2.962 points per set and Morgan Graves at 2.808. The losses are concentrated on the pins: Sariah Johnson (74.0 points in 2025, now at UC Riverside) and Morgan Castaneda (57.5). Roster churn was heavy anyway — 10 players departed against 9 returning, with one transfer in and four newcomers holding no DI record.

Santa Clara.summary: Five of six starters return for 2026, with 81% of production coming back and just one vacancy in the starting lineup — the outside hitter spot left by Layla Truitt, who led the team with 344.5 points in 2025. Everything else in the scoring order stays put: Cate Shanahan (3.565 points per set), Morgan Hayes (2.743), Grace Flanagan (2.47) and Selin Aslayan (2.46) are all back, running the same 5-1. The WCC side went 17-12 and took the conference's bid as regular-season champion, though the numbers underneath were softer, with a final RPI of 166. There are no incoming transfers, so the replacement for Truitt comes from within.

Seattle U.summary: Seattle U has to rebuild almost the entire front line: five of six starting spots are vacant, only one starter is back, and 10 players departed against 4 returning, leaving 28% of production. The exits are the top of the scoring sheet — Madyn Cervellera (426.0 points, to Washington St.), Yasemin Elmas (251.5, to UC San Diego) and Petra Fritz (247.0, to San Francisco) — and all three started at least 23 matches. Returning pieces are led by RS Teagan Melton at 2.127 points per set, OH Adee Butler at 1.722 and MB Taniyah Pruitt at 1.633, with 3 transfers in and 7 newcomers who have no DI record. The 2025 season finished 8-21 with an RPI of 309.

Seton Hall.summary: Seton Hall brings back its entire top scoring group, with outside hitter Sadie Reich (3.783 points per set) and Daria Safian (2.687) leading a returning class that accounts for 74% of production. The one real hole is middle blocker Asli Subasili, who started all 27 matches and scored 210 points before departing, leaving four of six starters back and a single vacancy in the starting six. The Big East team went 6-21 and finished 286th in RPI, so the returning core is rebuilding from a low base with just one transfer in.

Siena.summary: The outside hitting corps stays intact: Doga Diraz (3.854 points per set) and Gabrielle Wire (2.891) both return, as does Mary Claire Deacy (2.576). The losses are concentrated elsewhere — OH Elizabeth Phillips (258.0 points) and middles Ella Treasure (155.0, now at New Hampshire) and Berra Tok (130.5) all started at least 29 matches and are gone, leaving three starting-six vacancies. Six transfers arrive, including middles Lauren Stiles and Alison Goldberg, to fill a 5-1 that returns 70 percent of its production. The MAAC side went 14-19 and finished 313th in RPI.

South Alabama.summary: South Alabama brings back its top six scorers by points per set, led by outside hitter Cambria Gaier at 4.066 and Sarah Gooch at 3.892, with 73% of production returning. The holes are specific rather than broad: setter Anna Loberg and outside hitter Maradith O'Gorman, who started all 27 matches apiece and led the departures with 249 and 91 points, leave two vacancies in the starting six. The 5-1 offense will need a new distributor, and only one transfer has come in to fill it. The Sun Belt side finished 15-14 with an RPI of 101.

South Carolina.summary: Five of the six starting spots are open after nine departures, with only middle blocker Ava Leahy (26 starts) back from a lineup that went 10-16. The losses are concentrated on the pins: Alayna Johnson (303 points) and Nia Hall (299 points, now at Tennessee) both leave from the outside, and Emily Beeker (216 points) goes with them from the middle, leaving 26 percent of production returning. Five transfers in, including projected top scorer Olivia Borgman at 2.152 points per set, join returners Leahy (1.995) and Elise Marchal (1.879). The SEC team finished 86th in our final 2025 rank and 112th in RPI.

South Carolina St..summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after a 2-23 season, with 10 players departed and just 22% of production returning. The losses are concentrated at the pins and middle: Kiyah Felder (290 points), Hailey Harris (182) and Robyn White (156) are all gone, and Harris was one of two players to start all 19 matches with a known lineup. Setter Arianna James is back after 16 starts in the 5-1, alongside middle Jade Robinson (1.14 points per set), and transfer outside Jessika Martinez arrives as the highest-scoring name on the roster at 1.537. The MEAC side finished 337th in both our rank and RPI, and seven newcomers have no Division I record.

South Dakota.summary: Almost nothing left: 14 players return and 98% of production comes back, with just one departure, DS Kamryn Farris (42.0 points in 2025). The scoring core is intact from top to bottom — OH Lauren Medeck at 4.168 points per set, MB Morgan Bode at 2.995, OH Ava Ball at 2.932, MB Amanda Loschen at 2.704, MB Audrey Nelson at 2.327 and OH Samantha Laird at 2.293, all returning. South Dakota went 20-9 and took the Summit League's bid through the conference tournament, finishing 71st in our final rank and 72nd in RPI. There were no transfers in, with two newcomers who have no DI record.

South Dakota St..summary: The middle blocker room is the problem here: Sydni Schetnan (283.5 points) and Annalee Ventling-Brown (160.0) both leave after starting 27 and 26 matches, leaving three of six starting spots open. What comes back is the top of the attack, with Sylvie Zgonc at 4.769 points per set and an AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025, plus Madison Burr at 3.452 and setter Rylee Martin running the 5-1. South Dakota St. went 23-5 and took the Summit League's bid through the conference tournament, finishing 36th in RPI, and returns 73 percent of its production with two transfers in.

South Fla..summary: Roster turnover is the story here: 11 players departed against 5 returning, leaving 31% of production back and four of six starting spots open. The losses are concentrated on the pins and in the middle, with Maria Clara Andrade (519.0 points), Arianna Beckham (291.5) and Imani Hartfield (210.0) all gone, along with setter Raegan Richardson, who started 27 matches in the 5-1. What remains is real: Laila Ivey at 2.883 points per set, Addy Brus at 1.757 and Iyanna Garvin at 1.581 are all back, joined by 4 transfers in and 7 newcomers with no Division I record. The 17-13 season ended with a No. 46 RPI and an American tournament bid.

Southeast Mo. St..summary: Southeast Mo. St. reached the NCAA field the hard way, taking the OVC's bid through the conference tournament after a 21-13 season. The 2025 side ran a 5-1, with a serving order of Alandry Below, Reagan Nelson, Ramiri Gardner, Megan Holder, Lucy Arndt and Nina Schuberth. Lineup data is thin: only 11 matches had a known lineup, and Lucy Arndt (11 starts) led a rotation that also leaned on Ramiri Gardner (10) and Marin Johnson (9). The final RPI of 165 sat close to our own final ranking of 174, and no 2026 roster is posted yet for any of the listed starters.

Southeastern La..summary: A 20-9 season and a Southland tournament bid came from a lineup that is now largely gone: only one of the six main starters, setter Ashley Richardson, is back, leaving four vacancies in the starting six. The scoring picture is friendlier, since top scorer Kyra McKelvey (3.936 points per set, and an AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025) returns along with the rest of the top six scorers, but the departures of India Bennett (314.0 points) and Alexis Logarbo (289.5) take away most of the middle and right-side production. With 11 players returning, 48 percent of production back and no incoming transfers, the rebuild leans on six newcomers without a Division I record. The team finished 144th in our final ranking and 136th in RPI.

Southern California.summary: The top five scorers from a 25-7 season all return, led by London Wijay at 3.865 points per set and Abigail Mullen at 3.778, and returning production sits at 81 percent. The holes are specific rather than broad: three of the six starting spots are open, including setter Reese Messer, who started all 32 matches in the 5-1 before transferring to Kansas, and middle Rylie McGinest. Wijay was an AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025. Only one transfer came in against seven departures, so the setter job likely goes to someone already on the roster or one of the eight newcomers without a Division I record.

Southern Ill..summary: Southern Ill. returns none of its six starters, with all six from the 2025 lineup departed and 11 players gone in total, leaving just 3 returners and 12% of production. The losses are concentrated at the pins: outsides Kelly Franklin (385.5 points) and Annabelle Sulish (377.5) plus middle Larissa Seger (329.0) all scored heavily. Outside hitter Ella Swansiger is the top returning scorer at 2.054 points per set, and the roster adds one transfer and five newcomers without a DI record. The team went 13-17 in the MVC and finished 239th in RPI.

Southern Ind..summary: Southern Ind. brings back five of six starters and 79% of its production from a 19-13 season, with the only hole in the starting lineup at middle blocker after Bianca Anderson's 367.5 points departed. The top three scorers all return and all play outside hitter: Ashby Willis at 4.033 points per set, Carley Wright at 2.95 and Leah Coleman at 2.765. Setter Aysa Thomas is back after starting all 32 matches in the 5-1, and there are no incoming transfers to change the picture. The team finished 142nd in RPI and reached the field through the OVC tournament.

Southern Miss..summary: Southern Miss brings back five of six starters and 76% of its production from a 17-12 season, with the only hole left by outside hitter Brynn Botkin, who scored 322 points before departing. Sadie McAda anchors the returning group at 4.25 points per set and started all 28 matches, and the next five scorers — including middles Elly Stewart (2.28) and Lillie Johnson (2.227) — are all back. The Sun Belt team ran a 5-1 and finished 160th in RPI. Reinforcements are thin: one transfer in and three newcomers with no Division I record.

Southern U..summary: Five of the six starting spots are open after 11 players departed, leaving just one returning starter and 23% of production back. The biggest single hole is OH Ariana Brown, who accounted for 505.5 points in 2025 and led the serving order; MB Sophie Diouf (178.5 points) left for UT Martin. OH Zaria Nelson is the one returner from the starting six and the top scorer at 1.974 points per set. The 14-17 finish came with a No. 316 RPI, and the roster reload brings in 3 transfers, 2 of whom have no Division I record.

Southern Utah.summary: Southern Utah is essentially starting over: 13 players departed, only 2 return, and five of the six spots in the starting lineup are open. The one holdover from that group is outside hitter Kaitlyn Hoelker, who started all 23 matches and led the team at 2.077 points per set. The losses include opposite Victoria Zibecchi (255.5 points in 2025) and both starting middles, Kaitlyn Aleshire and Amaya Tobias, leaving returning production at 16 percent. The 5-1 team went 3-21 and finished 315th in RPI.

St. John's (NY).summary: Four of the six starting spots are open, including setter Erin Jones, who led the team with 351.5 points in 2025 before departing along with outside hitters Martina Ghezzi (275.0) and Ella Parker (203.0). What comes back is the middle: Chloe Bell at 2.106 points per set and Kya Harris at 1.464, plus opposite Kendall White at 1.663. With 34% of production returning, seven players gone and only one transfer in, the rebuild leans on five newcomers with no Division I record after a 10-19 season.

St. Thomas (MN).summary: St. Thomas (MN) brings back its top two scorers in outside hitters Anya Schmidt (3.643 points per set) and Ellie Gustafson (2.943), plus setter Morgan Kealy, giving the 5-1 four returning starters out of six. The departures are real, though: OH Tezra Rudzitis (426.5 points) and MB Megan Wetter (394.5) both started all 31 matches and are gone, leaving two holes in the starting lineup and 54 percent returning production. The 2025 season ended 21-10 with a conference tournament bid out of the Summit League and a final RPI of 73.

Stanford.summary: Stanford brings back five of six starters and 79% of its production from a 29-5 season, with the only real hole at outside hitter after Elia Rubin's 471 points departed. The returning core is unusually balanced: Julia Blyashov (3.517 points per set), Jordyn Harvey (3.145), Lizzy Andrew (3.033), Ipar Kurt (2.936) and Erika Sayer (2.854) all come back, along with setter Logan Parks in the 5-1. Andrew was an AVCA Second Team pick in 2025 and Parks earned Honorable Mention. The ACC regular-season champion finished 9th in RPI.

Stetson.summary: Stetson's top three scorers all return, led by outside hitter Zuzanna Bury at 4.614 points per set, with middles Xinlei Yang (2.752) and Kayla Balfour (1.876) behind her. The losses are concentrated elsewhere: setter Nyah Molina, who started 27 matches, and outside hitters Jenna Simmons (253.0 points) and Lilyanna Parker (141.5) are all gone, leaving 3 of six starting spots open. Nine players departed against six returning, though returning production still sits at 61 percent, with 2 transfers in and 7 newcomers who have no DI record. The 9-19 season ended with an RPI of 225 in the ASUN.

Stonehill.summary: The top four scorers by points per set all return, led by Sam Loyd at 2.724 and Abby Farrell at 2.312, which is how a 6-24 team ends up with 59% of its production coming back. The main departure is Mia Berardino, an outside hitter who accounted for 385.5 points in 2025 and started 28 matches. Setter Kendra Sawyer started all 29 matches in the 5-1 and returns, leaving three of six starting spots filled and one clear vacancy. Eight players left and nine return, with two transfers in and seven newcomers who have no Division I record.

Stony Brook.summary: Stony Brook ran a 5-1 in 2025 and leaned on a fixed core: setter Ava Zamora, middle Ayanna Pierre Louis and outside Kali Moore each started all 27 matches with a known lineup. Depth thinned quickly after that, with Mercedes Motton at 21 starts, Quinn Anderson at 17 and libero Carey-Jean Block at 14. The season ended 12-15, with an RPI of 175 and a final rank of 198. Rotation data is only partly settled — 57 of 123 resolved rotation sets agree — and no 2026 roster is posted yet for any of the listed starters.

Syracuse.summary: Syracuse ran a 5-1 in 2025 with a stable core: middle Soana Lea'ea started all 30 matches, with Gabby Mclaughlin and setter Tehya Maeva at 29 apiece and Skylar George at 27. The serve order stayed consistent enough that 28 of 135 resolved rotation sets agreed across 30 matches with a known lineup. The 13-17 record left the team at 156 in our final rank and 169 in RPI, in a season where the ACC's bid was awarded by regular-season champion. No 2026 roster information is available yet for any of the listed starters.

TCU.summary: TCU returns its entire outside hitter core — Evan Hendrix (4.933 points per set, 2025 AVCA Third Team), Becca Kelley (3.301) and Lauren Murphy (2.667) — which is the backbone of 67% returning production. The holes are in the middle: Sarah Sylvester (240.5 points) and Alexis Roberson (182.0, now at Houston) are both gone, leaving three of six starting spots open. The Big 12 regular-season champion went 21-11 and finished 20th in RPI, and brings in four transfers to fill the gaps.

Tarleton St..summary: Tarleton St. keeps its top scoring group intact: LaNeah Lara (2.791 points per set), Madison Frank (2.701), Alyssa Dinh (2.175) and Breannah Peterson (1.945) are all returning, part of 59% returning production from a 16-10 season that ended with a conference tournament bid. The losses are concentrated elsewhere, with Madison Natori Rice-Locket (261.5 points) and Emma Burke (243.0) gone among eight departures against nine returners. Three of six starting spots are open, and three transfers plus four newcomers without a Division I record arrive to fill them. The lineup picture is thin on evidence, with only one match of known lineup data and 25 of 113 rotation sets agreeing.

Temple.summary: Temple lost its top two scorers from a 16-15 season, with Leia Harper (398.5 points) and Alyssa Finister (317.0) both gone along with Katie Hickey (109.0), leaving three of six starting spots open. What returns is real, though: Christiana Greene led the team at 3.906 points per set and Olivia Hummel added 2.668, and Hummel started all 31 matches. Setter Lexi Yoza is back after 24 starts in the 5-1, and the lone transfer in, Khenedi Guest, scored 2.787 points per set. Returning production sits at 50 percent, with a final RPI of 133.

Tennessee.summary: Tennessee lost 12 players off a 20-8 team and returns just 35% of its production, with three of six starting spots vacant. Setter Caroline Kerr, an AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025, is back alongside middle Chelsea Sutton, who started 26 matches and scored 2.845 points per set. The rebuild leans on four incoming transfers: Jalyn Stout (3.849 points per set), Nia Hall (3.36) and Kennedi Rogers (2.962) all outproduced any returner. Departures include outside hitter Hayden Kubik, whose 431 points led the group that left.

Tennessee St..summary: Tennessee St. keeps its top scorers but loses the spine of the middle and the setter position: Maygan Miller-Garcia (264.0 points) and Aliyah Harris (215.5) both depart from MB, along with setter Sagaia Reilly (148.0), who started all 28 matches in the 5-1. What returns is the outside hitting — Carsyn Stansberry at 1.869 points per set and Melae Lacy at 1.557 — plus three of six starters, though returning production sits at 30 percent. A 1-30 record and a No. 345 RPI finish leave three starting-six vacancies to fill with 10 players gone and only 3 transfers in.

Tennessee Tech.summary: Tennessee Tech ran a 5-1 in 2025 with a stable core: OH Bella Powell and setter Jordan Karlen each started all 30 matches, with middles Jordyn Milhouse and Tuva Falk at 25 starts apiece. The lineup data is thin in places — of 141 rotation sets resolved, only 39 agreed, across 30 matches with a known lineup. The team finished 14-17, ranked 253rd in our final rankings and 235th in RPI, and reached the field through the SoCon tournament bid. No 2026 roster is posted yet, so returners, departures and transfers are all unlisted.

Texas.summary: Texas brings back five of six starters and 82% of its production from a 26-4 season, with the entire outside hitter and setter core intact. Torrey Stafford (5.277 points per set, AVCA First Team) and Cari Spears (3.573, Third Team) both return in the 5-1, as does setter Ella Swindle. The one hole is at middle: Ayden Ames, who started 26 matches and scored 207.5 points, left for Creighton, and with zero transfers in the replacement has to come from inside the program.

Texas A&M.summary: Texas A&M went 29-4 and finished with an RPI of 4, but the roster that produced it is largely gone: 8 players departed, only 24% of production returns, and 4 of the six starting spots are vacant. The losses are concentrated in the attack, with opposite Logan Lednicky (534.0 points), middle Ifenna Cos-Okpalla (396.5) and outside Emily Hellmuth (351.0) all off the roster. Kyndal Stowers, a 2025 AVCA Second Team pick, is back after 4.009 points per set, and the rebuild leans on 4 transfers in, including projected top scorer Natalie Ring at 5.162 points per set. The 5-1 system will need a new setter after Maddie Waak started all 33 matches.

Texas Southern.summary: Texas Southern returns its entire top scoring group, led by Lauren Battle at 2.13 points per set, Morgynne McQueen at 1.647 and Gracie Lee at 1.611. The losses are concentrated in two players: OH Gracie Hill (285.5 points in 2025) and MB Kourtni Collier (265.0), which leaves 2 vacancies in the starting six and 4 starters back. Depth comes from within rather than the portal, with 0 transfers in and 5 newcomers holding no DI record, against a 10-20 record and 55 percent returning production.

Texas St..summary: Almost the entire starting lineup is gone: only setter Anna Blaine, who started 16 matches, returns from the 2025 six, leaving 5 vacancies and just 15% of production back. The departures include OH Samantha Wunsch (440.5 points), MB Jade Defraeye (315.5) and OH Nina Moorer (295.0, now at Ole Miss). The rebuild leans on four transfers in, with MB India Bennett (3.413 points per set) and OH Peyton McKee (3.179) projected as the top scorers ahead of returning OH Britton Finley (2.4). Texas St. went 17-12 in 2025 and finished 45th in RPI, 62nd in our final rank.

Texas Tech.summary: Three of six starting spots are open after a 10-20 season, with outside hitters Kallista Jioshvili ravva (335.5 points) and Addie Kanouff (271.5, now at Washington) and middle Aliyah McDonald (152.5) all gone. What's left is still productive: returning outside Kenna McKenzie led the team at 2.764 points per set and middle Reagan Engler, a 10-match starter, added 2.727, with 47 percent of production back overall. The rebuild leans on volume rather than a marquee addition — 7 players departed, 8 return, only 1 transfer arrived, and 6 newcomers have no Division I record. The Big 12 team finished 172nd in our final rank and 189th in RPI.

The Citadel.summary: A 0-27 season did not empty the roster: The Citadel returns 10 players and 75% of its production, including four of six starters and its top five scorers. Rachel Reininger led the way at 3.591 points per set, with Gwen Berry at 2.418 and Sammie Sabra at 2.025, all outside hitters who are back. The departures are concentrated on the pins and middle, with Savannah Freeman (109.0 points) and Sam Barnes (74.0) gone, leaving two spots in the starting six. The SoCon team finished 336th in our final rank and 327th in RPI, and brings in one transfer plus five newcomers with no DI record.

Toledo.summary: Toledo won the MAC's automatic bid through the conference tournament and finished 23-11, but the 5-1 offense has to be rebuilt around a new setter after Kelsey Smith, a 34-match starter who led the departures with 219.5 points, left along with middle Anna Alford and outside Iremnur Elmas. Three of six starters return, leaving three vacancies, though 78 percent of production is back and 11 players return against four departures. The incoming class includes four transfers, among them outside hitter Ava Siefke at 3.836 points per set and middle Lilly Merk at 2.5, joining returning scorers Olivia Heitkamp (3.305) and Sierra Pertzborn (3.244).

Towson.summary: Towson went 21-7 and reached the NCAA field via the CAA tournament, but the roster turns over hard: four of the six starting spots are vacant, with only two starters back and 42% of production returning. The departures are the top three scorers by total points — Ella Sanders (379.5), Sarah Callender (344.0) and Erin Brothers (313.0) — who between them covered outside and middle. What returns is the top of the per-set list: Taylor Pagan at 3.109 points per set, Addison Leber at 2.61 and Malinah Purcell-Telefoni at 2.393, the last of whom started 27 matches at opposite. Setter is the open question after Maisie Jesse's 20 starts in the 5-1, with three transfers in and five newcomers who have no DI record.

Troy.summary: Troy returns four of six starters and 47% of its production, with outside hitters Kalina Calvillo (2.84 points per set) and Olivia Kwiatkowski (2.411) both back after starting 14 and 19 matches. The two vacancies come from OH Amiah Butler, who started all 23 matches and led the team with 450.5 points, and MB Sydney Austin, who started 20 and transferred to UAB. The roster churn is real — 7 departures against 8 returners, one incoming transfer and six newcomers with no Division I record. A 10-16 finish in the Sun Belt left them 167th in our final rank and 174th in RPI.

Tulane.summary: Avery Burks is the anchor here: an outside hitter who started 26 matches and led the team at 4.519 points per set, and she is back for 2026. The setter room is the question, with Ava Derbes gone after 253.0 points and 22 starts, though Zoe Rachow returns from 21 starts in the 6-2. Ten players departed against six returning, leaving 3 of six starters back and 2 vacancies in the starting lineup, with four transfers in. The 11-16 record came with a final RPI of 198.

Tulsa.summary: Tulsa returns its top four scorers by points per set — Olivia Vance (3.277), Jill Hanson (3.022), Kat Cooper (3.0) and Maegan Mills (2.313) — yet still has three vacancies in the starting six, with only three of six starters back. The departures are concentrated on the pins and at setter: outside hitters Lauren Eitler (326.0 points) and Beth Bayless (255.5) are gone, as is Brayden Hipp, who started all 32 matches running the 5-1. Returning production sits at 66 percent off a 25-7 season that ended with an RPI of 37 and an American Athletic bid earned through the conference tournament. Three transfers arrive alongside three newcomers with no Division I record.

UAB.summary: UAB kept its outside hitting intact: Mia Reese (3.333 points per set) and Abby Jones (2.702) both return, along with 4 of the six 2025 starters and 58% of production. The holes are in the middle and at opposite, where Jorda Crook (456 points, to Ole Miss) and Summer Snead (147.5 points, to Northern Colo.) departed, leaving 2 starting-six vacancies. The 13-15 record came with a conference tournament bid, and three transfers arrive to compete in the 5-1.

UAlbany.summary: UAlbany returns just 8% of its production after going 14-12, with only one of six starters back and five spots in the starting lineup open. The departures include the top three scorers by total points — Shynelle Woroniuk (428.0), Gabriella Karman (270.5) and Kendall Harris (253.0) — along with setter Maria Olga Siapani, who started all 26 matches in the 5-1. The highest-returning per-set scorer is outside hitter McKenna Collins at 1.286 points per set; libero Kiki Provatas, back after 14 starts, is the only returning starter. Two transfers arrive and three newcomers have no Division I record, so the America East rebuild is close to total.

UC Davis.summary: UC Davis brings back five of six starters and 67% of its production from a 21-7 season, with the only real hole left by outside hitter Jade Light, whose 474.5 points led the team by a wide margin. The top four returning scorers are all back, headed by Breeze Czapinski at 3.204 points per set and middle Ally Chandler at 2.952, and setter Mia Starr returns to run the 5-1. There are no transfers in, so the six newcomers with no DI record are the only outside additions. The Mountain West side finished 50th in our final rank and 49th in RPI after taking the conference tournament bid.

UC Irvine.summary: UC Irvine loses both middle blockers who started — Sydnee Rowe (200.5 points) and Ally Bolden (169.0, off to William & Mary) — plus outside hitter Kendra Duffey, whose 369.0 points led the departures, leaving three of six starting spots open. What comes back is the setter room and the perimeter: setter Nicole Feliciano started all 31 matches and returns, and the top four scorers by points per set, led by Jessica Bates at 3.354 and Kendra MacDonald at 2.765, are all listed as returning. That still adds up to only 44 percent returning production after a 13-18 season that finished 211th in RPI. The roster churn is real — 8 departures against 8 returners, one transfer in and seven newcomers with no Division I record.

UC Riverside.summary: Five of the six starting spots are open after ten departures, including all three of last year's top point scorers — Sophia Ewalefo (379 points), Mia Delahoussaye (219) and Layla Hooks (175). Only 24% of production returns, with Andrea Brewer the lone returning starter and the top returning scorer at 2.556 points per set. Three transfers arrive, two of whom (Sariah Johnson and Madison Pulsipher) would slot straight into the outside hitter rotation vacated by the departures. The Big West team went 9-19 in 2025 and finished 274th in RPI.

UC San Diego.summary: A 6-24 season in the Big West left UC San Diego 241st in our final rank and 273rd in RPI, but the roster holds together better than that record suggests: 4 of the six starting spots return, along with 56 percent of production. The 6-2 offense is the reason two setters, Ireland McNees and Maija Nepszy, both appear among the top scorers, with McNees at 3.009 points per set behind outside hitter Molly McCluskey's 3.904. McCluskey started all 30 matches. The departures are concentrated in the middle and on the pin, with Jasmine Saran (266.5 points) and Maria Fernanda Afonso (251.0) both gone.

UC Santa Barbara.summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after a 23-9 season, with only 2 of six starters back and 30% of production returning. The departures are the top of the attack: Eva Travis (424 points, off to Wisconsin), Kiersten Schmitt (339), and Layanna Green (334), all regular starters in the 5-1. The rebuild leans on four transfers in, including Auburn Tomkinson at 2.711 points per set and Bella Mathis at 2.24, alongside returning outside Gabi Martinez at 3.241. The Big West side finished 51st in RPI and reached the field through the conference tournament.

UCF.summary: Avah Armour carried the offense at 4.886 points per set, more than double the next scorer, and she returns after taking AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025. UCF brings back four of six starters and 67 percent of its production from a 17-12 season, with the two departures both outside hitters — Skylar English (336.5 points) and Reaghan Thompson (253.5). That leaves two holes in the starting six alongside setter Abby Schomers, who ran the 5-1 and started 27 matches. The middle tandem of Sasha Cohen (2.29) and Ella Chapman (2.021) is intact.

UCLA.summary: The top three scorers all return: middle Marianna Singletary at 3.262 points per set, with outsides Maggie Li (2.727) and Eliana Urzua (2.719), and setter Kate Duffey is back after 31 starts in the 5-1. The losses are concentrated in two spots — outside Cheridyn Leverette (511.0 points) and middle Brooklyn Briscoe, who started all 32 matches before leaving for Florida — leaving two vacancies in the starting six. Overall, 4 of six starters and 49% of production return from a 19-13 season that ended with a No. 35 RPI. Three transfers arrive to fill the gaps.

UConn.summary: Almost the entire starting lineup is gone: only one of six starters returns, leaving five vacancies and 18% of production back after 11 departures. The losses are led by outside hitter Emma Werkmeister (496 points in 2025) and middle Audrey Rome (297 points), who went to Cincinnati. The rebuild leans on transfers, with Maja Daca projected as the top scorer at 3.631 points per set alongside returning outside Grace Maria at 1.871. The Big East team went 19-9 and finished 74th in RPI, reaching the field via the conference tournament.

UIC.summary: Every one of the six players who started most often in 2025 has departed, leaving all six spots in the starting lineup open and just 25% of production returning. The losses are concentrated at the pins and middle: Ayat Amin (318.5 points), Cleo Lorenzo (285.5) and Julieta Sandez (280.0) all go. What comes back is thin but not empty — middle Ana Petrides at 2.278 points per set and outside Gabi Peter at 2.154 are the top returning scorers, though the roster added no transfers and brings in nine newcomers without a Division I record. The 2025 team went 17-10 and reached the field through the MVC tournament.

UIW.summary: UIW ran a 5-1 in 2025 with a stable core: setter Calissa Allison and middle Vanessa Eregie each started all 27 matches with a known lineup, and Finley Evans and Kyla Malone started 26 apiece. The 17-13 record was enough to reach the NCAA field via the Southland tournament bid, with a final RPI of 135 close to our final rank of 131. Rotation data is thin — only 51 of 180 resolved rotation sets agreed — and no 2026 roster has been posted, so every listed starter is currently unaccounted for.

ULM.summary: ULM heads into 2026 with 14 players departed and only 5 returning, though the pieces that stayed are the useful ones: Aniya Hall (3.965 points per set), middle Kenzie Behl (1.867) and setter Morgan Howard, who started all 26 matches in the 5-1. Three of the six starting spots are open, with outside hitters Kennedy Plummer (237.5 points, off to West Florida) and Madison Derden (185.0) both gone. The rebuild leans on 4 transfers in and 8 newcomers with no Division I record, and returning production sits at 40 percent. The 2025 season finished 10-20 with an RPI of 276.

UMBC.summary: UMBC brings back five of six starters and 90% of its production from a 13-12 season, with the only real hole at setter after Izzy Ostvig (136.5 points) departed from the 5-1. The returning group is heavily outside-hitter driven: Jalynn Brown (4.15 points per set), Hannah Dobbs (3.072) and Claudia Llamas (2.995) are all back, along with middle Helen Frankovich (1.936). The America East team earned its bid through the conference tournament and finished 171st in RPI. One transfer arrives, plus five newcomers with no Division I record.

UMES.summary: UMES ran a 5-1 in 2025 and leaned on a settled front line: middle Anjola Omolewa started all 29 matches, with outside Karielys Melendez at 28 and setter Jayda Hutchins at 27. The serving order was consistent enough that lineups were known in all 29 matches, though only 13 of 170 resolved rotation sets agreed. The 11-18 finish came with an RPI of 294 and a final ranking of 304, and the MEAC bid was awarded by conference tournament. No 2026 roster is posted yet for any of the top starters.

UNC Asheville.summary: UNC Asheville is essentially rebuilding from scratch: 14 players departed against 6 returning, leaving 17% of production and only 2 of six starters back. The three biggest losses were all outside hitters — Kylie Cackovic (345.5 points in 2025, now at Northern Colo.), Albertine van der Goot (281.5) and Ana Djurovic (271.0). What's left is led by OH Addie Brookbank at 2.556 points per set and MB Lydia Pate at 1.727, with the next returning scorers well under a point per set. The Big South side went 12-18 and finished 231st in RPI, and has four starting-six vacancies to fill with one transfer in and five newcomers with no DI record.

UNC Greensboro.summary: Allie Sweet is the engine here: an outside hitter who started all 28 matches and scored 5.018 points per set, far clear of anyone else on the roster. Four of the six starters are back from a 17-12 season, with 60 percent of production returning in a 5-1 offense, though the two departures at outside hitter, McKenna Timmerman (349.0 points) and Robin Rosser (316.0 points), leave two holes in the starting six. Middle blockers Connore' Siler-Nixon (2.145 points per set) and Siena Smiejek (1.902) also return, and the SoCon program adds one transfer plus four newcomers with no Division I record.

UNCW.summary: UNCW is rebuilding almost from scratch: 11 players departed and only 4 return, leaving 23% of production and just one of six starters (MB Lilly Sullivan, 23 starts) back for 2026. The losses include the top three scorers by points in 2025 — Hannah Forbes (267.0), Marnie Ursem (244.5, now at Hawaii) and Avery Markham (164.5) — all of whom were regular starters. Five transfers arrive, and three of them (Courtney Graham at 2.539 points per set, Sam Vanda at 1.746, Gaby Zovko at 1.014) project as the top of the new scoring order alongside Sullivan at 1.693. The CAA team went 5-21 last season and finished 285th in RPI.

UNI.summary: UNI brings back 12 players and 90% of its production from a 26-6 season, including five of six starters and its top six scorers. The one hole is at middle blocker, where Lindsay Oldendorf (188.5 points) left for Illinois; there are no incoming transfers to replace her. Cassidy Hartman, an AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025, led the offense at 4.638 points per set with fellow outside Lily Dykstra at 4.071, both returning to the 5-1. The MVC side finished 24th in RPI and reached the field via the conference tournament.

UNLV.summary: UNLV brings back five of its six starters and 75% of its production from a 13-15 season, including Jaida Harris, who started all 28 matches and led the team at 4.181 points per set. The one hole is at outside hitter, where Alondra Alarcon left after 360 points and 27 starts. Behind Harris, the returning group includes Basia Latos (2.481 points per set), Rheanna Deen-Jackson (2.37) and Brooklynn Williams (2.182), all back in a 5-1 run by setter Kaia Thiele. The Mountain West side finished 169th in our final rank and 194th in RPI, with just one transfer in and five newcomers without a Division I record.

USC Upstate.summary: All six of USC Upstate's top scorers return, led by outside hitter Summer Kohler at 3.894 points per set and middle Kensley Haneline at 2.926, with 14 players back and 75% of production retained. The only meaningful departure is middle blocker Ady O'Grady, who scored 429 points in 2025 and opened the serving rotation. There were no incoming transfers, so the Big South group that went 14-14 and finished 249th in RPI is essentially intact rather than rebuilt.

UT Arlington.summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after a 11-14 season, with only two starters back and nine players departed. The losses are concentrated on the pins: Jalie Tritt (370.0 points) and Sophie Ocampo (203.0, now at Troy) were both outside hitters, and setter Mira Ledermueller, who started 24 matches in the 5-1, is also gone. What returns is scoring — Camryn McMinn at 2.724 points per set, Sophia Krichev at 2.228 and Evyn Snook at 2.352 — plus 44 percent of overall production and two incoming transfers.

UT Martin.summary: Four of the six starting spots are open after a 4-25 season, with both outside hitters and the setter gone; Kayla Bryant (352.5 points) and Kylie Surratt (284.5, now at Youngstown St.) led the departures, along with opposite Kristin Phillips (228.0). Only 27 percent of production returns, headlined by opposite Maddy Gladson at 2.016 points per set and middle Carly Mueller at 1.658, the one returning starter who played a full-time role. The four incoming transfers include Sophie Diouf at 1.962 points per set and Luli Arcucci at 1.514, both middles, so the rebuild is concentrated on the pins and at setter. The OVC bid comes through the conference tournament, which matters for a team that finished 332nd in RPI.

UTEP.summary: A 25-5 season that ended with a conference tournament bid leaves this Mountain West side rebuilding four of six starting spots, with only 33 percent of production returning. The departures are the scoring core: outsides Torrance Lovesee (384.5 points) and Sara Pustahija (333.0) plus middle Danika Washington (243.5), all of whom started nearly every match. What comes back is setter Kalia Kohler and outside Landry Braziel, who led the team at 2.399 points per set, alongside returning scorers Luvina Oguntimehin (1.98) and Hannah Crowe (1.906). Roster churn is heavy: seven departed, one transfer in, and six newcomers with no DI record.

UTRGV.summary: The top four scorers all return, led by outside hitter Martina Franco at 4.042 points per set and Nadine Zech at 3.092, but the setter spot is open after Isabella Costantini left for Arizona St. UTRGV also loses Dimitra Nanou, whose 346.5 points in 2025 led the departures, to BYU. Four of six starters are back and returning production sits at 57 percent, with two starting-six vacancies to fill from two transfers in and four newcomers without a Division I record. The 22-8 season, run out of a 5-1, ended at 82 in RPI and 94 in the final ranking, with the conference bid decided by the Southland tournament.

UTSA.summary: UTSA brings back five of six starters and 80% of its production from a 13-15 season, including Ally Tribe (3.101 points per set) and Caroline Tredwell (2.861), who both started all 28 matches. The one hole in the lineup is outside hitter Taylor Gaines, who scored 269 points before transferring to Louisiana. Five transfers arrive to fill out a roster that ran a 5-1, and the group finished 156th in final RPI.

Utah.summary: Utah went 15-15 while claiming the Big 12 regular-season champion bid, and it enters the offseason with four of six starting spots open. Kamryn Gibadlo, an AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025, is the anchor: she led the team at 4.703 points per set and started all 29 matches, and she returns. The departures are heavy up front, with middle Emrie Moea'i (418.5 points) and outside hitters Neea-Maria Joki (255.0) and Levani Key-Powell (179.5) all gone. Nine players return, along with two transfers in, but only 52 percent of production comes back.

Utah St..summary: Utah St. returns none of its six starters from a 24-8 season, leaving all six spots in the starting lineup open and just 2% of its production back. The departures include the top three scorers by points — Mara Stiglic (494), Loryn Helgesen (453, now at Utah) and Tierney Barlow (392) — all of whom also occupied serving slots in the 5-1. The rebuild runs through the portal: 7 transfers in, and the projected top scorers are led by Sami Blackett at 3.574 points per set, with middle Ava Napierski (1.45) the lone returner among them. The team finished 21st in final RPI after taking its bid through the conference tournament.

Utah Tech.summary: Utah Tech brings back five of six starters and 78% of its production from a 21-6 season, with the only hole at middle blocker after Taylor Snow's 260 points departed. Kennedi Knudsen anchors the returning offense at 4.85 points per set, backed by Casidy Fried (2.459) and Nana Asiata (2.37), both of whom started at least 22 matches in the 5-1. The Big Sky bid came through the conference tournament, and the final RPI rank of 92 matched where the team was rated.

Utah Valley.summary: Almost nothing carries over here: 10 players departed against 6 returning, five of the six starting spots are vacant, and returning production sits at 10 percent. The 2025 group went 16-11 with an RPI of 120 and reached the NCAA field through the Big West tournament, but the entire top of the scoring sheet — Avery Page (409 points), Sami Blackett (361) and Bella Wooden (276) — is gone. Olivia Gloeckner, the one returning starter, is the only holdover among the leading scorers at 1.974 points per set; transfers Miley Thunstrom (2.4) and Brielle Rueckert (1.832) headline a rebuilt front row, with two transfers in and four newcomers who have no Division I record.

VCU.summary: VCU comes back with four of its starting six to replace, including opposite Julia Rienks (504.0 points in 2025) and outside hitters Kalina Pylinska (311.0) and Alicja Jaryszek (244.5), leaving 43 percent of production returning. What is left is heavily middle-blocker shaped: Letizia Galli (2.491 points per set) and Sarah Dibbs-Frantz (1.993) are the two returning starters, alongside Nina Boledovicova (2.277) in the middle. The top returning scorer overall is opposite Lara Del Core at 3.628 points per set. With no transfers in and six newcomers who have no Division I record, the 16-13 team has to rebuild the pins from inside the program.

Valparaiso.summary: The top three scorers all return: Ava Helming (3.576 points per set), Jordyn Gove (2.693) and Jessica Pickett (2.217), which is unusual for a team that also has three of six starting spots to fill. The departures are real ones — Sam Warren (365.0 points in 2025), Lilly Merk (265.0, now at Toledo) and Kadence Brumitt (250.5) — and setter Addy Kois is gone from the 5-1 as well. This is a 21-9 group that took the MVC's bid through the conference tournament, finishing 138th in RPI, with 10 players back and returning production at 50 percent. Two transfers arrive alongside five newcomers with no DI record.

Vanderbilt.summary: Vanderbilt ran a 5-1 in 2025 behind setter Isabella Bareford, who started all 27 matches, as did middle Jacquelyn Moore and outside Reese Animashaun. The lineup was otherwise unsettled: Kayla Dunlap started 22 matches, Kamryn Chaney 16 and libero Elli Kinney 12, and rotation data resolved 129 sets with only 18 in agreement across 27 matches with a known lineup. The 9-18 record landed at No. 118 in final RPI and No. 83 in our final ranking, with the SEC's automatic bid awarded by conference tournament. No 2026 roster is posted, so none of the listed starters are confirmed back.

Villanova.summary: All six starters return from a 20-8 season, leaving zero vacancies in the starting lineup and 91% of production back. The lone meaningful departure is opposite Ava Mehrten, who scored 160.5 points in 2025; everything else that mattered stays, including Abby Harrell (4.313 points per set) and Campbell McKinnon (3.51) in a 5-1. The Big East team earned its bid through the conference tournament and finished 39th in RPI.

Virginia.summary: Reagan Ennist is the anchor here: an outside hitter who started 26 matches and led the team at 4.186 points per set, and she's back. Three of the six starters return, leaving three spots in the starting lineup open after the departures of Kadynce Boothe (238 points in 2025), Jasmine Robinson (164) and Kate Dean (144). Two transfers arrive with scoring history, Emily Fowler at 3.17 points per set and Reese Wuebker at 2.852, which matters for a 13-17 group running a 5-1. Returning production sits at 64 percent.

Virginia Tech.summary: Ten players departed and only 20% of production returns, leaving four of six starting spots open after a 12-19 season. The losses are concentrated at the pins and middle: Payton Woods (366.5 points, off to Arizona), Isabella Mishler (260.5) and Brianna Holladay (224.0, to Florida) all started at least 28 matches. Setter Camilla Brandalise is back after starting all 30 matches in the 5-1, as is outside Reese Hazelton at 2.176 points per set, and incoming transfer Destiny Walker brings a 4.455 points-per-set profile. The ACC group finished 209th in our final rank and 234th in RPI.

Wake Forest.summary: Wake Forest ran a 5-1 in 2025 and leaned on a stable core: Paige Crawford started all 31 matches at outside hitter, with Sanaa Williams (30 starts) and Kelis Hawkins (27) in the middle. The result was a 15-16 record, a No. 146 RPI and a No. 109 finish in our rankings, despite the ACC's bid going to its regular-season champion. Roster information for 2026 is not yet available, so returners and departures cannot be assessed. Lineup confidence is limited as well: of 134 rotation sets resolved, only 47 agreed.

Washington.summary: Washington loses both outside hitters who anchored the pin, Kierstyn Barton (447.5 points in 2025, now at San Diego) and Alexa Markley (393.0), plus setter Alexis Haury, leaving three starting-six vacancies and 44% returning production. What comes back is the middle and one outside: Simona Mateska led the team at 3.477 points per set, with Julia Hunt at 2.25 and Katy Wessels at 2.004, and Wessels started all 30 matches. The 13-17 record came with a conference tournament bid, and the profile finished 47th in our final rank against a 57 RPI. Two transfers arrive, including Addie Kanouff at 2.403 points per set, to help fill a 5-1 that must replace its setter.

Washington St..summary: Washington St. is rebuilding most of a lineup: only 2 of six starters return, leaving 4 starting-six vacancies and 34% of production back after 8 departures and 7 transfers in. The losses are concentrated at the front row, with middle Lucie Blazkova (384.0 points in 2025) and outside hitters Melina Christodoulou (270.0) and Taryn Vrieling (228.5) all gone. The incoming scoring is expected to come from transfers Emerson Matthews (4.149 points per set) and Madyn Cervellera (3.737), with returning outside Eliana Ti'a (2.75) as the holdover. The 5-1 team went 17-11 and finished 154th in RPI.

Weber St..summary: Weber St. has to rebuild most of a lineup that went 18-12 and won the Big Sky's automatic bid through the conference tournament, with only 2 of six starters back and 4 starting-six vacancies to fill. The departures are concentrated in the attack: outside hitters Kaylie Ray (353.0 points) and Ashley Gneiting (325.5) and middle Saane Munyer (204.0) are all gone, leaving returning production at 33 percent. Opposite Rose Moore, who led the team at 3.986 points per set and started 28 matches, is the anchor, with libero Marly Pratt back after 27 starts. Two transfers arrive alongside 6 newcomers with no Division I record.
