West Ga..summary: West Ga. ran a 5-1 in 2025 and leaned on a fixed group: middles Alex Strating and Sanai Young started all 28 matches with a known lineup, with Grace-Blythe Cornett (26), Valiree Schmus (25) and setter Addy Franz (24) close behind. The results did not follow, a 2-27 record that left the team 324th in our final rank and 323rd in final RPI, in a UAC that awards its bid through the conference tournament. Roster status for 2026 is unresolved: no players are listed as returning or departed, no transfers in, and each of the top starters is flagged no_roster. The rotation data is also thin, with only 32 of 128 resolved rotation sets in agreement.

West Virginia.summary: West Virginia keeps its top three scorers — Nina Horning (3.364 points per set), Trinity Sheridan (3.162) and Maddy McGath (2.363) — and returns four of six starters, with 66% of production coming back from a 15-15 season. The losses are concentrated on the pins: Cassidy Tanton (250.5 points) and Laila Ibrahim (199.5) leave two holes in the starting six. There are no incoming transfers and eight newcomers without a Division I record, so the replacements will be unproven. The Big 12 side finished 90th in RPI and 93rd in our final rank.

Western Caro..summary: Five of six starters return from an 8-21 season, including setter Katie Boney, Samantha Kranzler and Tatum Sharp, who each started all 29 matches in the 5-1. The only hole in the starting six is at middle, where Courtney Graham (261.5 points) left for UNCW and fellow MB Janelle Blue (224.5) also departed. The top three scorers by points per set — Zoe Zudans at 3.22, Sharp at 3.168 and Kranzler at 2.678 — are all back, part of 63 percent returning production. With one transfer in and five newcomers without a DI record, the SoCon team closed 2025 at 271 in RPI.

Western Ill..summary: The top five scorers by points per set all return, led by outside hitter Kennedy Adair at 2.441 and middle Hillary Estes at 1.653, yet returning production still sits at 43 percent because Keyana Cruse's 454 points walked out the door. Three of the six primary starters are back, leaving three vacancies in the starting lineup, and there are no incoming transfers to fill them. Western Ill. went 7-24 in the OVC while running a 5-1, finishing 326th in final RPI.

Western Ky..summary: Western Ky. brings back its top six scorers, led by Kaira Knox at 3.935 points per set and Alivia Skidmore at 3.745, which is a big reason returning production sits at 89 percent with 10 players back. The losses are concentrated at setter and middle: Callie Bauer (131.5 points in 2025) and Gabby Weihe (62.5, now at Western Mich.) leave two holes in the starting six, with four starters returning. The 27-6 season ended with a No. 30 final RPI and a conference tournament bid out of CUSA.

Western Mich..summary: Western Mich. loses its entire middle-blocker core: Mary Clare Brusek (391.0 points), Molly Brown (344.5) and Amanda Glanton (240.0) all depart, leaving three vacancies in the starting six. What comes back is the outside and the setter — Annalise Patchett at 2.907 points per set, Mia Jurkovic at 2.424, and Leah Richmond, who started all 31 matches in the 5-1. Returning production sits at 38 percent after a 17-16 season that finished 141st in RPI.

Wichita St..summary: Wichita St. brings back its top six scorers from a 19-11 season, led by outside hitter Sydney Dunning at 4.164 points per set and middle Maddie Wilson at 2.586. Four of six starters return, including setter Jordan Heatherly in the 5-1, leaving two vacancies after the departures of Brooklyn Leggett (441.0 points) and Emerson Wilford (233.5). Returning production sits at 64 percent, with 11 players back, six gone and one transfer in. The American bid came through the conference tournament, and the season closed at No. 58 in our final rank against an RPI of 59.

William & Mary.summary: William & Mary keeps its top three scorers — Audrey Brcka (3.121 points per set), Katherine Arnason (3.01) and Devereaux Hoxsie (2.86), all outside hitters — but has to rebuild the middle of the lineup and the setter spot. Departures include opposite Nicole Smith (269.0 points in 2025), setter Beatriz Silva (98.5) and middle Ryann Love (87.0), leaving three of six starting spots open with 62 percent of production returning. The CAA team went 12-15 last season and finished 222 in RPI, running a 5-1 offense.

Winthrop.summary: Both opposites who started all 25 matches are gone: Avery Jolley (430.5 points in 2025) and Rachel McCollum (214.5 points, now at UAB), leaving two vacancies in the starting six. What comes back is the middle and the pin scoring — Paige Bennett at 3.443 points per set, Teagan Sychterz at 2.51 and Giselle Little at 2.26 — with four of six starters and 60% of production returning. The 18-7 record earned a Big South bid through the conference tournament, with an RPI of 111.

Wisconsin.summary: Wisconsin went 28-5 and finished eighth in the final RPI after taking a Big Ten bid via the conference tournament, but the roster that produced it is largely gone: nine players departed and only 23% of production returns. Four of the six starters are gone, including Mimi Colyer (659.0 points in 2025), Una Vajagic (340.5) and Carter Booth (317.0), leaving four vacancies in the starting six. Setter Charlie Fuerbringer, a 2024 AVCA Third Team pick, returns alongside outside hitter Grace Egan, who scored 2.905 points per set. Two transfers project as the top scorers: Eva Travis at 4.417 points per set and Jaela Auguste at 3.505.

Wofford.summary: Wofford brings back 14 players and 82% of its production from a 17-14 season, including four of six starters and the top four scorers by points per set: Chloe Smith (3.889), Bradley Brown (3.375), Natalie Arnold (2.403) and Ella Coleman (1.859). The two holes are middle blocker Annemarie Rakoski, who started all 31 matches and led the team with 281.5 points, and defensive specialist Caroline Przystup. The SoCon team, which reached its bid through the conference tournament, ran a 5-1 and finished 129th in RPI.

Wright St..summary: Five of six starters return from a 21-11 season that ended with a Horizon League tournament bid, including the top three scorers: outside hitters Mya Ayro (4.34 points per set) and Katie Sowko (3.807) and middle Reilly Zegunis (2.983). The one hole is middle blocker Taylor Bransfield, who started 31 matches and led the team with 300.5 points before departing. There are no incoming transfers, so the 72% returning production has to carry a 5-1 offense run by setter Lauren Yacobucci, a 32-match starter.

Wyoming.summary: Wyoming ran a 5-1 in 2025 and reached 17-13 while claiming its Mountain West bid through the conference tournament. Lineup continuity was strongest at the pins and middle: OH Paige Lauterwasser and MB Sarah Holcomb each started all 30 matches, with setter Sara Quigley starting 22. The rotation data is only partly settled — of 150 rotation sets resolved, 60 agree — so the serve order beyond the core six is less certain. No 2026 roster information is available for any of the listed starters.

Xavier.summary: Xavier brings back five of six starters and 13 players from a 26-5 team that took the Big East's automatic bid through the conference tournament, with 61% of its production returning. The top three scorers all return: middle blockers Margo Kemp (2.624 points per set) and McKinley Boehm (2.338) plus outside hitter Charlotte Moriarty (2.433). The losses are concentrated on the pin, where Emma Grace (429 points) and Anna Taylor (321) both depart, leaving one vacancy in the starting six for the 5-1. The roster adds one transfer and four newcomers with no Division I record.

Yale.summary: Yale's top four scorers by points per set all return, led by outside hitter Ava Poinsett at 4.234 and middle Laurece Abraham at 3.324, which is why 73 percent of production comes back despite three of six starting spots being open. The departures are concentrated at setter and in one middle slot: Halle Sherlock ran the 5-1 and started 15 matches, while Gigi Barr started 16 and scored 119.5 points. There are no incoming transfers, so the new setter and the third front-row spot will come from inside a group that went 15-9 in the Ivy League.

Youngstown St..summary: Abbie Householder is the engine here: an outside hitter who started all 31 matches, scored 4.727 points per set, and picked up AVCA Honorable Mention in 2025. She and setter Kameron Blizniak, also a 31-match starter, anchor a 5-1 that returns 3 of six starters and 51 percent of its production. The departures are real — Gabriela Machin (443.0 points) and Taya Nordmann (199.5, to Jacksonville St.) are gone, leaving 3 holes in the starting lineup — but three transfers in, led by Kylie Surratt at 2.845 points per set, arrive to fill them. Youngstown St. went 17-14 and finished 241st in RPI.
